item.title: Neurocognitive function and quality of life results from a phase II study (NRG/RTOG 0424) of temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy regimen for high-risk low-grade gliomas.
item.dc:creator: Wefel JS, Pugh SL, Choucair AK, Fisher BJ, Rogers CL, Mikkelsen T, Glass J, Yu HM, Robins HI, Won M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Wefel JS, Pugh SL, Choucair AK, Fisher BJ, Rogers CL, Mikkelsen T, Glass J, Yu HM, Robins HI, Won M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.031
Published: 2026-Nov-08
PMID: 43000083



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This analysis of NRG/RTOG 0424 describes post-treatment changes in neurocognitive function (NCF) and quality of life (QOL) in patients with high-risk low-grade glioma (HR-LGG). METHODS: Patients with HR-LGG were treated with radiation and concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide (RT-TMZ). Standardized NCF tests were performed at baseline, 6, and 12 months. Rates of change in NCF were examined using the reliable change index (RCI) on Hopkins Verbal Learning Test (HVLT), Trail Making Test (TMT), and Controlled Oral Word Association (COWA). Relationships between NCF and subjective cognitive concerns (MOS-CF) were evaluated. QOL was assessed using Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy - Brain (FACT-Br). Longitudinal modeling evaluated predictors of change in NCF and QOL. Cox models assessed the association of baseline NCF with overall survival (OS). RESULTS: From January 2005 to August 2009, 129 evaluable patients were accrued, and 93 completed at least the baseline and one post-treatment NCF/QOL measurement. RCI-determined decline occurred in 50% and 40% at 6 and 12 months, respectively and was most frequent on HVLT (21%, 20%), TMTA (29%, 20%), and TMTB (22%, 14%). MID-determined QOL decline on the FACT-Brain Subscale occurred in about 25% at 6 and 12 months. Several tumor and clinical characteristics were associated with worse NCF including tumor crossing the midline, the number of high-risk factors, and EORTC OS risk group. CONCLUSIONS: Many patients with HR-LGG experience NCF decline in the first year after treatment with temozolomide-based concurrent chemoradiation. QOL remained stable or improved. Ongoing studies with integrated NCF monitoring using these tests will aid clinicians and patients in treatment decisions that seek to consider oncologic and functional outcomes.

item.title: The Transformation of Oncology Drug Development in China: Toward a New Phase of Innovation.
item.dc:creator: Chen Y, Liu D, Song Y, Luo Y, Shi C, Zeng H, Peng H, Xie Y, Cao C, Yuan Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Chen Y, Liu D, Song Y, Luo Y, Shi C, Zeng H, Peng H, Xie Y, Cao C, Yuan Y, et al.
Journal: Cancer discovery | DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-26-1628
Published: 2026-Nov-08
PMID: 42999985



Abstract:
UNLABELLED: China's oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value-driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

item.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
item.dc:creator: Motovska Z, Hlinomaz O, Mrozek J, Akin I, Kala P, Montalescot G, Hromadka M, Geisler T, Precek J, Kettner J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Motovska Z, Hlinomaz O, Mrozek J, Akin I, Kala P, Montalescot G, Hromadka M, Geisler T, Precek J, Kettner J, et al.
Journal: Lancet (London, England) | DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00976-1
Published: 2026-Nov-07
PMID: 42998670



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS. METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor. INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS. FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

item.title: Global Proposal for the TNM Staging System for Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Shi X, Liu Q, Scholfield D, Li D, Lamartina L, Chen S, Zhang H, Papachristos AJ, Hamdy O, Timofeeva N, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shi X, Liu Q, Scholfield D, Li D, Lamartina L, Chen S, Zhang H, Papachristos AJ, Hamdy O, Timofeeva N, et al.
Journal: JAMA oncology | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4705
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42994809



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC) lacks a dedicated staging system, requiring use of the eighth version of the American Joint Committee on Cancer and Union for International Cancer Control TNM staging system (TNM-8) for differentiated thyroid cancer despite its distinct biology. OBJECTIVE: To develop a PDTC-specific staging system. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed data from the International Aggressive Thyroid Cancer Collaborative Group (IATCCG), including surgically treated patients at 91 centers in 14 countries from January 1984 to January 2026. External validation was performed using patients from the US Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to June 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was overall survival. With M1 disease predefined as stage IVB, the schema for stages I-IVA in patients with M0 disease were redefined. All possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion defining the proposed system. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and C statistics. RESULTS: Among 1010 patients in the IATCCG cohort, 610 (60.4%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 58 (46-68) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 41 (15-85) months. Among 170 patients in the SEER cohort, 85 (50.0%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 61 (49-72) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 92 (42-154) months. In the IATCCG cohort, level VII lymph node metastasis (LNM) was associated with lower 5-year overall survival (45.2%; 95% CI, 33.4-61.2) than level VI (73.2%; 95% CI, 64.4-83.3) or lateral neck LNM (56.7%; 95% CI, 49.4-65.0). Level VII LNM was therefore reclassified from N1a to N1c. The lowest Akaike information criterion configuration among 16 738 candidates defined stages I to IVA as follows: I, T1N0/NX/N1a or T2N0/NX; II, T1N1b/N1c, T2N1a/N1b, or T3N0/NX/N1a; III, T2N1c, T3N1b, or T4aN0/NX/N1a; IVA, T3N1c, T4aN1b/N1c, or T4b any N; and IVB, M1 disease. Compared with TNM-8, stage I disease decreased from 44.4% (448 of 1010) to 24.6% (248 of 1010) and stage IV disease increased from 18.5% (187 of 1010) to 32.4% (327 of 1010) with the proposed system. The proposed staging had a higher C statistic than TNM-8 (0.74 [95% CI, 0.71-0.76] vs 0.71 [95% CI, 0.68-0.74]; difference, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.04). Corresponding SEER C statistic values were 0.76 (95% CI, 0.71-0.81) vs 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79), respectively (difference, 0.02; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.06). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study found that this PDTC-specific staging system provides improved prognostic stratification reflecting its different biology. These data provide a strong rationale for the potential inclusion of a stand-alone American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system for PDTC.

item.title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
item.dc:creator: Harada S, Koyama Y, Kobayashi Y, Imai T, Yoshioka Y, Kobayashi H, Inohara H, Shimada S
item.description:
Authors: Harada S, Koyama Y, Kobayashi Y, Imai T, Yoshioka Y, Kobayashi H, Inohara H, Shimada S
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361954
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993734



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models. METHODS: We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis. RESULTS: The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.

item.title: Protocol for investigating the association between Helicobacter pylori exposure, antigen-specific serological responses, and resistant versus non-resistant hypertension in a South African cohort.
item.dc:creator: Mennen MC, Zulu MZ, Mabatha KC, Baguma R, Skelem S, Mbundwini NN, Aremu OO, Adriaanse M, van Dijk D, Pillay P, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Mennen MC, Zulu MZ, Mabatha KC, Baguma R, Skelem S, Mbundwini NN, Aremu OO, Adriaanse M, van Dijk D, Pillay P, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362215
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993715



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.

item.title: A systematic review of Moringa oleifera seed toxicity and safety: Comparative analysis of toxicology methodologies and results.
item.dc:creator: Russell JJ, Pritchard M, Paterson AWJ
item.description:
Authors: Russell JJ, Pritchard M, Paterson AWJ
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360006
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993711



Abstract:
This systematic review aims to assess the reliability of contemporary toxicological research on Moringa oleifera seeds. Academic databases were browsed on a yearly basis (2014-2024); identification and screening were conducted between July 17th 2023 and January 13th 2025. Primary research reports on M. oleifera seed toxicology were included for data collection. Fifty-three fields were used to collect data. Data was synthesised by comparing methodological data points to contemporary toxicity testing guidelines; results were presented as a narrative synthesis. Conflict of interest, research quality and risk of bias were assessed using Cochrane tools modified for non-human laboratory studies. Thirty-seven non-duplicate publications were identified, of which 14 were included for data collection. In total, 395 data points were collected and synthesised. Financial conflicts of interest were declared in one report. Nine reports received "lower quality" or "lowest quality" research quality judgements. Six reports received "high risk of bias" judgements. Bias risk was commonly associated with selective reporting of data. M. oleifera seed toxicity was commonly tested via rodent study. Seven rodent studies included an acute toxicity test and nine included a sub-acute toxicity test. Two acute oral toxicity tests returned LD50 values of 14,000-15,000 mg/kg bw. Three sub-acute oral toxicity tests returned NOAEL values of 100-257 mg/kg bw/d. Oral LD50 and NOAEL data could only be derived from reports with "lowest quality" research and/or "high risk of bias" judgements, so these safety limits are unreliable. Inadequate dosing schemes were the primary cause of limited LD50 and NOAEL data. Dose range non-compliance also caused unnecessary animal suffering. To facilitate standardisation in future research, several guideline-based methodological recommendations are made. Determining reliable safety limits for M. oleifera seed consumption may reduce incidence of acute kidney injury, thereby supporting Targets 3.4 and 3.d of the United Nations sustainable development goals.

item.title: Testing the effects of nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims on oral nicotine pouch packaging engagement, self-reported perceptions and use intentions, and product trial in young adults and adults: Protocol for a randomized trial.
item.dc:creator: Long L, Alalwan MA, Alvarado E, Kozar A, Stevens EM, Shang C, Roberts ME, Klein EG, Shoben A, Mays D
item.description:
Authors: Long L, Alalwan MA, Alvarado E, Kozar A, Stevens EM, Shang C, Roberts ME, Klein EG, Shoben A, Mays D
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362172
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993708



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited. OBJECTIVES: We outline the protocol for a randomized trial examining how nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims affect engagement with ONP packaging using psychophysiological measures, self-reported ONP perceptions and use intentions, and ONP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06192316). METHODS: Between 2024 and 2027, we will recruit 450 participants, comprised of: 150 young adults ages 18-24 who are susceptible but do not use tobacco; 150 young adults ages 18-24 who use tobacco; and 150 adults ages 25-65 who use tobacco. Participants complete procedures at an in-person laboratory visit. During the visit, participants complete pre-exposure self-report measures and are randomized between subjects to one of nine conditions in a 3 (Nicotine Concentration: None, Low, or High) x 3 (Nicotine Source Claim: None, Tobacco Free, or Synthetic) design. Within conditions, participants view 16 ONP pack images, in random order, reflecting different ONP brands and flavors. During exposure, we collect psychophysiological measures including heart rate, skin conductance, and visual attention. After exposure, participants complete self-report measures of ONP perceptions and use intentions, and a timed behavioral task where they are presented with ONP packages corresponding to their randomized condition and brands and flavors shown in the stimuli. Participants can try one of the products, and ONP trial is the behavioral outcome of interest. However, the packages do not contain ONPs; they contain commercially available pouches with food grade ingredients. At visit conclusion, participants are de-briefed and receive their incentive for participating. CONCLUSIONS: This project will generate evidence on the effects of nicotine concentration and source claims on ONP packaging in young adults who are not using but susceptible to tobacco, young adults using tobacco, and adults using tobacco to inform potential regulations.

item.title: Tumor Longevity: a time-dependent biomarker of immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness across head and neck, lung, renal and urothelial cancers.
item.dc:creator: Romanò R, Airoldi C, Alfieri S, Piemontese A, Pierri S, Calvanese G, Piscazzi D, Ciarlo G, Signorelli D, Pizzutilo EG, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Romanò R, Airoldi C, Alfieri S, Piemontese A, Pierri S, Calvanese G, Piscazzi D, Ciarlo G, Signorelli D, Pizzutilo EG, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag445
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42992952



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: the duration of tumor persistence within the host-defined as Tumor Longevity (TL) - may capture cumulative biological and immunologic interactions, shaping immunotherapy treatment response. However, the impact of TL on outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) remains unexplored. We hypothesized that TL may reflect integrated tumor-host dynamics influencing ICI efficacy and investigated this association in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), renal and urothelial cancer (R/UC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: we conducted a retrospective, observational study including adult patients with advanced HNSCC, NSCLC, R/UC receiving ICI (≥first line) across 2 Italian cancer centers. TL, defined as the time from first histological diagnosis to ICI initiation, was analyzed as a continuous variable using 3-knot restricted cubic spline models. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses assessed associations between TL and disease control rate (DCR), grade (G)≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: 304 patients, diagnosed from 2002 to 2022, started ICI from 2014 to 2022. Median TL was 15.30 months (IQR 5.52-33.05). Overall DCR was 56.25% [95% CI 50.47; 61.91]; CTCAE G ≥ 3 irAEs occurred in 16 (5.2%) patients; 231 (76.0%) patients died. In multivariable analyses, longer TL was associated with higher DCR (OR Q3 vs. Q1 = 3.26; 95%CI 1.24; 8.59, p = 0.004), while no significant associations for G ≥ 3 irAEs (OR = 1.27; 95% CI 0.39-4.12) and OS (HR = 0.79; 95% CI 0.49-1.28; p = 0.407) were observed. CONCLUSIONS: These real-world, hypothesis-raising results suggest that TL may capture clinically relevant information associated with ICI outcomes. TL may represent a pragmatic, time-dependent biomarker integrating tumor behavior and host factors. Prospective and translational studies incorporating TL with molecular and immune profiling are warranted to elucidate whether this association reflects tumor biology, host factors, treatment history, or their combination.

item.title: Early Post-Market Surveillance of Bimodal Neuromodulation for Tinnitus.
item.dc:creator: Srivatsa A, Gathman TJ, Stefan A, Agabigum B, Chan E
item.description:
Authors: Srivatsa A, Gathman TJ, Stefan A, Agabigum B, Chan E
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70513
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42992588



Abstract:
The Lenire system uses bimodal auditory and tongue stimulation to treat tinnitus. FDA-approved since 2023, the device has shown efficacy and safety in initial trials. Using the MAUDE database, we conducted preliminary post-market surveillance. This retrospective review analyzed reports of the Lenire device from 2023 to 2025. Event characteristics were examined for initial trends. The MAUDE database has limitations, including underreporting and reporting bias. Nine unique reports related to the Lenire device were extracted from MAUDE. The most commonly reported events included tinnitus exacerbation (n = 6), no tinnitus improvement (n = 2), and fatigue (n = 1). There was a single death from suicide temporally associated with device use and preceded by episodic tinnitus worsening, then overall improvement, but causality could not be established. Five patients had sustained tinnitus exacerbation after device discontinuation and were reportedly unaware of the potential treatment-related adverse effect. The findings, although limited by reporting bias and lack of validation, have identified reports of users who may experience adverse effects, including tinnitus exacerbation that may continue even after device discontinuation.

item.title: Endoscope-Assisted Transoral Resection for Pharyngeal and Laryngeal Vascular Malformations: A Surgical Technique.
item.dc:creator: Iwasaki M, Ueha R, Goto T, Sato T, Koyama M, Ishizuka R, Rameau A, Kondo K
item.description:
Authors: Iwasaki M, Ueha R, Goto T, Sato T, Koyama M, Ishizuka R, Rameau A, Kondo K
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70509
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42992577



Abstract:
Pharyngolaryngeal vascular malformations (PLVMs) are commonly treated with sclerotherapy; however, its efficacy for localized protruding lesions is often limited and may require multiple sessions with a risk of airway edema. We describe an endoscope-assisted transoral technique using flexible-tip endoscopy and tailored laryngoscopic exposure for safe, function-preserving resection. This technique was applied in 7 patients with PLVMs. Surgical exposure was achieved using an FK-WO retractor or curved laryngoscope, and visualization was provided by a flexible-tip rigid endoscope. Resection was performed along the submucosal plane while avoiding intralesional incision. All procedures were completed successfully with minimal blood loss and no postoperative complications. Oral intake was resumed within 3 postoperative days, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up. Endoscope-assisted transoral resection provides a safe and effective treatment for selected PLVMs. This approach allows precise lesion control while preserving function and may represent an alternative to repeated sclerotherapy in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Work productivity impairment and its associated factors among patients with cancer in Bangladesh: a hospital-based cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Mothashin M, Khatun R, Hossain MT, Al Mamum ASM, Hossain MG
item.description:
Authors: Mothashin M, Khatun R, Hossain MT, Al Mamum ASM, Hossain MG
Journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice | DOI: 10.1007/s11764-026-02150-x
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42989027



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer imposes substantial physical, psychosocial, and economic burdens on affected individuals, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where out-of-pocket healthcare financing remains dominant. Despite these challenges, evidence on work productivity impairment among patients with cancer in Bangladesh is limited. This study aimed to evaluate work productivity impairment and identify the factors associated with it among cancer patients in Bangladesh. METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 patients with cancer receiving treatment or follow-up care at two tertiary-level hospitals in Bangladesh: Rajshahi Medical College Hospital and Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Work productivity impairment was assessed using the validated Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) questionnaire, with overall work impairment derived from absenteeism and presenteeism scores. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participants' characteristics and work productivity outcomes, while beta regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with overall work impairment. RESULTS: The mean absenteeism, presenteeism, and overall work impairment scores were 38.1%, 49.7%, and 63.3%, respectively. Overall, work productivity impairment was substantial, with presenteeism contributing more to productivity loss than absenteeism. Beta regression analysis showed that older age (β = 0.028, p < 0.001), higher levels of occupational physical activity (β = 0.032, p = 0.028), having lung cancer (β = 1.208, p < 0.001), prostate cancer (β = 1.139, p < 0.001), and other cancers comprising skin, liver, laryngeal, hematological, bone, and cervical cancers (β = 0.721, p < 0.001) compared with thyroid cancer, being diagnosed with stage II cancer (β = 0.389, p = 0.011) compared with stage I and a longer duration since diagnosis (β = 0.101, p = 0.012) were significantly associated with greater work impairment. In contrast, higher educational attainment was significantly associated with lower work impairment (β = - 0.039, p = 0.018). CONCLUSION: Cancer patients in Bangladesh experience substantial work productivity impairment, highlighting a severe dual functional and financial burden. Both clinical and socio-demographic factors significantly influenced productivity loss. The findings underscore the urgent need for affordable cancer care, workplace accommodation policies, and strengthened financial risk protection mechanisms to reduce the economic and occupational consequences of cancer in Bangladesh. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Targeted support can help cancer survivors maintain work productivity, reduce financial hardship, and improve quality of life.

item.title: A Global Perspective on Calibration and Standardization in Oral Cancer Screening Training.
item.dc:creator: Zain RB, Ramanathan A, Ghani WMN
item.description:
Authors: Zain RB, Ramanathan A, Ghani WMN
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70559
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989832



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early oral cancer detection improves survival, but diagnosing early, asymptomatic lesions remains challenging. Screening effectiveness depends heavily on examiner competency, highlighting the need for structured training and calibration. OBJECTIVE: This narrative review examines the evolution, current practices, and future directions of examiner training, calibration, and standardization in global oral cancer screening. REVIEW FINDINGS: Existing training programs vary widely in content, duration, and assessment. While structured approaches combining theoretical instruction, image-based learning, and supervised clinical training enhance diagnostic accuracy, published studies provide limited details on training protocols, calibration procedures, and competency benchmarks. Formal assessment of inter-examiner reliability, periodic recalibration, and standardized quality assurance are inconsistently reported. Models like OralDETECT demonstrate scalable, competency-based frameworks. Additionally, empowering community health workers through artificial intelligence, mobile health, and adjunctive diagnostic tools provides promising opportunities to expand screening capacity in resource-limited settings. CONCLUSION: Establishing an internationally standardized framework for examiner training, competency assessment, and continuous quality assurance is essential to improve screening reliability and reduce global oral cancer mortality. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Structured training and calibration bridge critical diagnostic gaps among primary healthcare practitioners. Integrating these standardized protocols with digital health innovations enhances triage accuracy, overcomes geographic barriers, and optimizes risk-based screening models.

item.title: Systemic Therapies for Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis: A Systematic Review of Efficacy and Safety.
item.dc:creator: Sánchez Sáez G, Gómez García FJ, Ruíz Roca JA, Galera Molero F
item.description:
Authors: Sánchez Sáez G, Gómez García FJ, Ruíz Roca JA, Galera Molero F
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70560
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989707



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of systemic pharmacological and nutritional interventions for recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched for studies published from 2001 to 2026. Clinical trials and analytical observational studies of systemic treatments for RAS were included. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Twenty studies were included: 16 randomized trials, three non-randomized intervention studies, and one observational cohort. Interventions included corticosteroids, colchicine, thalidomide, levamisole, pentoxifylline, dapsone, clofazimine, sulodexide, montelukast, roflumilast, rebamipide, vitamin B12, vitamin C, multivitamins, zinc, and omega-3 fatty acids. Several therapies improved pain, ulcer burden, healing, or recurrence-related outcomes, but comparative evidence was inconsistent. Thalidomide showed potential benefit but important safety limitations and a high risk of bias. Nutritional interventions showed mixed results. CONCLUSIONS: Selected systemic therapies may benefit severe, frequent, or refractory RAS, but no intervention can be considered clearly superior. Evidence certainty is limited by heterogeneity, small samples, limited direct comparisons, and risk of bias.

item.title: Direct Oral Healthcare Costs Associated With Xerostomia and Hyposalivation: A Scoping Review and Annual Cost Synthesis.

Authors: Dutra MJ, Martins MD, Dame-Teixeira N, Wagner VP
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70565
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989595



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the available evidence on direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia and hyposalivation. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science, with additional screening of gray literature. Studies reporting direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia or/and hyposalivation were eligible. Reported costs were standardized to a common currency and price year. Exploratory annual cost scenarios were generated by combining reported unit costs with reported guideline-based or hypothetical frequencies. RESULTS: Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Six (75%) were conducted in the United States and two (25%) in the United Kingdom. Reported cost components included dental consultations, salivary stimulants and substitutes, restorative treatments, dental implants, fluoride applications, and management of oral infections. Evidence was heterogeneous in populations, etiologies, healthcare settings, cost components, and reporting methods. Illustrative base-case scenarios ranged from USD 3296.08 to USD 10,414.51 per patient per year (USD 1791.23-5658.99 when hypothetical events and possible overlaps were excluded). CONCLUSION: The evidence base is limited and heterogeneous. The exploratory annual synthesis provides an initial framework for mapping reported cost components but does not represent a definitive estimate of economic burden.

item.title: Metronomic Tegafur-Uracil Maintenance Therapy in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Following Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Lu HJ, Chiu YW, Tseng HC, Peng CY, Hsin CH, Chuang CY, Wu MF, Huang WS
item.description:
Authors: Lu HJ, Chiu YW, Tseng HC, Peng CY, Hsin CH, Chuang CY, Wu MF, Huang WS
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70563
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989576



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) is the predominant subtype of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan. Despite the guideline-recommended adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for advanced pathological risk factors, long-term survival remains suboptimal. We evaluated the efficacy of tegafur-uracil as metronomic maintenance therapy following adjuvant CRT. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 197 OCSCC patients who underwent curative resection followed by adjuvant CRT. Patients were stratified by receipt of metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: Patients receiving metronomic maintenance therapy (49.2%, 97/197) demonstrated favorable survival trends compared with those who did not. Five-year disease-free survival and disease-specific survival rates were 57.4% vs. 53.0% (p = 0.101), and 70.1% versus 60.8% (p = 0.092), respectively. Patients with ≥ 2 risk factors-extreme body mass index, positive margins, extranodal extension, and advanced depth of invasion-demonstrated significantly better outcomes following metronomic maintenance therapy. Therapy initiation at 1-3 months post-CRT and a treatment duration exceeding 12 months were also associated with a better prognosis. CONCLUSION: Metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy was associated with favorable outcomes, particularly in patients presenting with ≥ 2 identified risk factors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

item.title: Reconstructing Skull Base Reconstruction: The State of the Art.
item.dc:creator: El Shatanofy M, Sargi Z, Nisenbaum E
item.description:
Authors: El Shatanofy M, Sargi Z, Nisenbaum E
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70538
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989572



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull base reconstruction has continued to evolve in parallel with advances in endoscopic skull base ablation in order to accomplish the goal of restoring larger and more complicated defects between the cranial and nasal cavities while balancing morbidity, cost, and recovery. METHODS: We reviewed recent literature on advances in skull base reconstruction including graded endoscopic reconstruction, appropriate use of perioperative adjuncts, endoscopic free tissue inset, patient-specific planning, dural substitutes, regenerative scaffolds, and autologous biologics. RESULTS: Graded reconstruction supports free grafts or local flaps for selected low-flow defects and multilayer vascularized closure for high-flow defects. Lumbar drainage benefits selected high-risk patients, whereas routine packing and prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis are not consistently supported. Endoscopic free flap inset, virtual surgical planning, and patient-specific implants expand options for complex composite and salvage defects. Synthetic dural substitutes can reduce donor-site morbidity in appropriate cases. Leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) has emerging clinical support, while most regenerative scaffolds, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), and cell-based strategies remain preclinical. CONCLUSIONS: With advancements in skull base reconstruction, the paradigm has shifted toward using the least morbid construct that reliably restores the intracranial-sinonasal barrier while preserving function and quality of life. Standardized, prospective studies with attention to patient- and value-centric outcomes are crucial for improving care. Material science advances will continue to expand reconstructive options.

item.title: Laryngeal Cancer Microbiome Study Reveals Parvimonas and Campylobacter as Potential Therapy Targets.
item.dc:creator: Lad H, Shah A, Thompson ER, Javid S, Chee RH, Zaransky S, Dhanda A, Mudhar A, Lamichhane S, Chua AT, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lad H, Shah A, Thompson ER, Javid S, Chee RH, Zaransky S, Dhanda A, Mudhar A, Lamichhane S, Chua AT, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71027
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989377



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Laryngeal cancer accounts for 40% of head and neck malignancies and 1% of all cancer-related deaths worldwide. We evaluated the laryngeal cancer microbiome to identify cancer-specific genera as potential treatment targets. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted using 57 laryngeal mucosal samples from 24 treatment-naive laryngeal cancer patients and 33 patients who were undergoing otolaryngological surgery unrelated to oral or laryngeal diseases (01/2023-09/2025). DNA was extracted and amplified in triplicate, targeting the V3/V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene, followed by paired-end 2 × 300 bp sequencing on the Illumina NextSeq 2000. Amplicon sequence variants were identified via DADA2 and assigned to genera using a naive Bayes classifier. Two samples with zero classified read pairs were excluded. RESULTS: Most patients were male (87.5% cancer, 66.7% controls) and smokers (83.3% cancer, 54.5% controls). Cancer patients' core laryngeal microbiomes uniquely contained Parvimonas (3.67%; 95% CI: 0.70%-6.64%), and Campylobacter (1.12%; 95% CI: 0.60%-1.63%), while control patients' uniquely contained Corynebacterium (2.97%; 95% CI: 0.00%-7.67%) and Alloprevotella (1.34%; 95% CI: 0.64%-2.04%). Cancer samples were significantly enriched in 19 genera, notably Peptococcus (2.93, q = 0.0003), Campylobacter (1.68, q = 0.009), and Parvimonas (2.02, q = 0.03), compared to controls. CONCLUSIONS: Laryngeal cancer patients' samples displayed microbial dysbiosis, with enrichment of microbes present in gastrointestinal cancers, cervical cancer, and inflammatory states; they also exhibited loss of immunoprotective taxa. These findings support that microbiome profiling can distinguish malignant mucosa and guide future studies targeting genera increased in cancer, including Parvimonas and Campylobacter.

item.title: Opposing microbiome-mediated axes link modifiable lifestyles to health and chronic diseases.
item.dc:creator: Nagata N, Wei R, Kaneko G, Nishijima S, Aoki R, Kojima Y, Tamura Y, Sugiyama M, Hamabata T, Nakagawa T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Nagata N, Wei R, Kaneko G, Nishijima S, Aoki R, Kojima Y, Tamura Y, Sugiyama M, Hamabata T, Nakagawa T, et al.
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04744-5
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42988934



Abstract:
Analyses disentangling the role of the gut microbiome in linking lifestyle factors to health outcomes remain limited. Here, using fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort, we identified two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases. A health-associated axis enriched in microbial metabolism of dietary components was linked to plant-based, soy and dairy intake. In contrast, a disease-associated axis, enriched in oral-derived bacteria and pathobionts, was linked to refined carbohydrates and sedentary behavior. Starter culture microorganisms used to ferment foods did not show statistically significant mediation of the observed health effects. Alcohol was associated with both health- and disease-oriented mediation patterns involving microbial host-glycan utilization. Microbiome-defined health- and disease-oriented mediator axes were supported by fecal short-chain fatty acids and plasma cytokines from >1,700 individuals, revealing butyrate-associated anti-inflammatory and pro-inflammatory host profiles, respectively. Microbiome-based prediction (MADE) scores captured lifestyle-microbiome-disease mediation patterns and distinguished individual diseases across 13 independent external cohorts from the United States, China, Sweden, Russia and Australia. We identify the gut microbiome as a key mediator linking lifestyle to health and disease, providing a framework for microbiome-based assessment to guide lifestyle interventions for health promotion and disease prevention.

item.title: Elective Neck Dissection in cT1-4 N0M0 Submandibular Gland Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Patel AM, Pamula SD, Mehari M, Lingam SR, King ZD, Bharadia AP, Czerwonka L, Vanison CC
item.description:
Authors: Patel AM, Pamula SD, Mehari M, Lingam SR, King ZD, Bharadia AP, Czerwonka L, Vanison CC
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70998
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42988768



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate occult nodal metastasis (ONM) and overall survival (OS) in patients undergoing elective neck dissection (END) for clinically node-negative submandibular gland cancer (SMGC). METHODS: The 2006 to 2018 National Cancer Database was retrospectively reviewed for patients with cT1-4 N0M0 SMGC undergoing surgical resection. Linear, binary logistic, Kaplan-Meier, and Cox proportional hazards regression models were implemented. RESULTS: A high proportion of patients were female (N = 710, 54.6%) and White (N = 1059, 82.5%) with adenoid cystic carcinoma histology (N = 567, 43.6%) classified as cT1 (N = 545, 41.9%). A minority of patients (N = 255, 19.6%) underwent END. Academic/research reporting facility, high grade, cT3, and cT4 classification were associated with higher odds of undergoing END; Medicare insurance was associated with lower odds (p < 0.05). ONM was identified in 63 (24.7%) patients undergoing END. The rate of ONM increased with cT classification (13.2% in cT1, 27.9% in cT2, 22.0% in cT3, and 50.0% in cT4) and grade (6.5% in well-differentiated, 9.5% in moderately differentiated, and 40.3% in poorly differentiated). END was not associated with OS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-1.46, p = 0.461). However, ONM was associated with worse OS (HR 3.69, 95% CI, 2.25-6.05, p < 0.001); 5-year OS for patients without and with ONM was 83% and 50%, respectively (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: END is performed frequently in SMGC but is not associated with OS. Although the rate of ONM approaches 25%, these findings suggest that END should not be routinely performed for prognostic purposes alone, especially in the absence of adverse features.

item.title: Cepstral Peak Prominence and Pitch Strength as Acoustic Indicators of Dysphonia in Children.
item.dc:creator: Fujiki RB, Nudelman CJ
item.description:
Authors: Fujiki RB, Nudelman CJ
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71023
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42988763



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the extent to which Cepstral Peak Prominence Smoothed (CPPS) and pitch strength differentiate between healthy and dysphonic pediatric voices using sustained vowels and connected speech. METHODS: Voice samples were collected from 100 children between the ages of 4 and 12 years (mean = 7.8, SD = 2.4, 48% female). Forty-two children presented with benign vocal fold lesions, and 58 had no history of voice complaint. CPPS and pitch strength were calculated on sustained vowels and connected speech. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations between acoustic measures and voice-disorder status. Receiver operating characteristic analyses quantified classification accuracy and identified optimal thresholds. RESULTS: Children with voice disorders demonstrated significantly lower CPPS and pitch strength values on sustained vowel and connected speech when compared to vocally healthy controls. CPPS on sustained vowel was the strongest predictor of voice status; however, all measures effectively separated children with and without voice disorders. Despite significant group-level differences, substantial within-group variability limited the establishment of clear diagnostic cutoffs. Optimal thresholds for differentiating children with and without voice disorders were 11.19 dB for CPPS on sustained vowel (95% CI = 10.58-12.29), 9.48 dB for CPPS on connected speech (95% CI = 8.98-10.06), 0.30 for pitch strength on vowel (95% CI = 0.27-0.35), and 0.28 for pitch strength on connected speech (95% CI = 0.25-0.28). CONCLUSIONS: Findings support the use of CPPS in routine pediatric voice assessment and identify pitch strength as a promising adjunctive metric. Incorporating brief cepstral and pitch-based analyses into standard clinical protocols may enhance objectivity while minimizing testing burden in children.

item.title: Skull Base Osteoradionecrosis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: Long-Term Outcomes of Vascularized Flaps.
item.dc:creator: Xu X, Ong YK, Loh KS
item.description:
Authors: Xu X, Ong YK, Loh KS
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71041
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42988578



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Skull base osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a late but debilitating complication of previously irradiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Patients often suffer from chronic pain and recurrent bleeding, which can culminate in a carotid blowout. This study examines the natural history of skull base ORN over a long follow-up, and the outcomes with conservative and surgical management. METHODS: A retrospective review (June 2011 to December 2025) of radiated NPC patients with skull base ORN managed at a tertiary center was performed. Outcome measures were symptom control, incidence of carotid blowout and survival. RESULTS: There were 28 patients with a follow-up of 23.0 (14.0-31.0) years. Signs of ORN developed at 14.0 (6.0-23.0) years after radiotherapy. The most common symptom was recurrent bleeding (85.7%). The incidence of carotid blowout was 53.6%. Survival after ORN diagnosis was 5.0 (2.0-8.0) years. Eighteen patients (64.3%) were managed conservatively. Ten patients (35.7%) underwent endoscopic debridement and vascularized flap reconstruction. Patients who underwent surgery had better symptom control, lower incidence of carotid blowout (20.0% vs. 72.2%, p = 0.008) and longer overall survival (29.0 [10.0-31.0] vs. 21.5 [14.0-36.0] years, p < 0.001) than those managed conservatively. CONCLUSIONS: Survival after skull base ORN diagnosis was generally poor. Conservative management was associated with poorer symptom control and frequently progressed to carotid blowout eventually. Early recognition of ORN and timely surgical debridement with vascularized flap reconstruction in appropriately selected patients may provide better symptom control, reduce progression to carotid blowout, with a potential survival benefit.

item.title: The Association Between Muscle Health and Quality of Life in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Zuijlen T, van Lint L, Preissner C, de Bree R, Speksnijder CM
item.description:
Authors: Zuijlen T, van Lint L, Preissner C, de Bree R, Speksnijder CM
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70542
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42988558



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) are at risk of impaired muscle health due to metabolic disturbances, reduced nutritional intake, and treatment-related toxicities. Because muscle health supports physical capacity and independence, its decline may affect quality of life (QoL). This systematic review examined the association between muscle health and QoL in patients with HNC. METHODS: Studies were included if they involved patients with HNC, used validated muscle health and QoL measures, and examined their association. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. Poorer muscle health was associated with lower global QoL, poorer physical and role functioning, greater fatigue, swallowing difficulties, restricted mouth opening, social eating problems, and salivary toxicities. Methodological limitations and heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Poorer muscle health was associated with worse QoL in patients with HNC, although this evidence does not establish causality. Prospective studies using standardized measures are needed. item.title: Identification of Plasmodium sporozoites using angle-resolved scattered light pulse shapes.
item.dc:creator: Devaraj V, Kahler S, Kage D, Levashina EA, Kaiser T
item.description:
Authors: Devaraj V, Kahler S, Kage D, Levashina EA, Kaiser T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0354060
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42986815



Abstract:
Flow cytometry is widely used to identify and sort rare cells, but conventional approaches rely on fluorescent labels. Label-free discrimination of rare targets in complex, heterogeneous samples remains challenging. Here, we introduce a label-free strategy that combines multi-angle pulse shape flow cytometry (MAPS-FC), which exploits the full temporal structure of the signal pulses during cell or particles transit through the laser spot, with a deep learning-based analysis. As a biologically relevant test case, we focus on Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites, the infectious stage of the malaria parasite, which need to be isolated from mosquito salivary glands and are embedded in a heterogeneous mosquito-derived background. Using a GFP-expressing reporter line for validation, we trained a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network to classify sporozoites solely from their scattering pulse shapes captured through MAPS-FC. Using training data from multiple days and setting a threshold on the classification confidence, the network can distinguish sporozoites from mosquito debris without fluorescent labels. This work establishes MAPS-FC with deep learning as a platform for label-free identification of rare parasites in complex biological samples.

item.title: Fine Particulate Matter Exposure and Sinonasal Malignant Neoplasm.
item.dc:creator: Yang HH, Hwang PH, O'Sharkey K, Grimm DR, Franks ZG
item.description:
Authors: Yang HH, Hwang PH, O'Sharkey K, Grimm DR, Franks ZG
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3453
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42986618



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Exposure to fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less (PM2.5) has been associated with multiple malignant neoplasms, but its relationship with sinonasal malignant neoplasm (SNM) remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between regional PM2.5 exposure and first observed SNM diagnosis. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This national case-control study used commercial outpatient claims with eligible index dates from January 2007 to December 2020. Cases were defined by the first eligible SNM diagnosis after a 1-year enrollment washout period. Controls without any SNM diagnosis throughout claims history were randomly sampled at an approximate 1:5 case to control ratio. Regional PM2.5 exposure was derived from NASA 1-km gridded models integrating satellite, meteorologic, land-use, and atmospheric data, aggregated to each participant's residential metropolitan statistical area and index date. Associations were evaluated using mixed-effects logistic regression with a metropolitan statistical area-level random intercept, adjusted for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, regional smoking prevalence, and socioeconomic deprivation. The analysis was conducted from March 2025 to August 2026. EXPOSURES: Mean regional PM2.5 exposure during the 6-month, 1-year, and 5-year periods preceding the index date. MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: First observed SNM diagnosis after a 1-year enrollment washout period. RESULTS: The analytic cohort included 21 295 individuals: 3600 patients with SNM (mean [SD] age, 51.5 [10.6] years; 1656 [46.0%] female and 1944 [54.0%] male participants) and 17 695 controls (41.5 [14.0] years; 9663[54.6%] female and 8032 [45.39%] male participants). Mean (SD) PM2.5 concentrations were higher among cases than controls across the 6-month (8.57 [2.52] vs 8.36 [2.50] μg/m3), 1-year (8.69 [2.45] vs 8.45 [2.43] μg/m3), and 5-year (9.36 [2.67] vs 9.08 [2.67] μg/m3) windows. In fully adjusted models, each SD increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of first observed SNM diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.05-1.49] for 6-month average exposure, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.08-1.59] for 1-year average exposure, and 1.36 [95% CI, 1.11-1.66] for 5-year average exposure). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this case-control study, greater regional PM2.5 exposure was associated with higher odds of a first observed SNM diagnosis, with larger estimates for longer averaging windows. Further epidemiologic and mechanistic investigation is warranted.

item.title: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy for Head and Neck Cancers With Perineural Spread.
item.dc:creator: Lawless AK, Goodman CD, Wang CH, Wang XW, Frank SJ, Fuller CD, Garden AS, Gunn GB, Moreno AC, Morrison WH, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lawless AK, Goodman CD, Wang CH, Wang XW, Frank SJ, Fuller CD, Garden AS, Gunn GB, Moreno AC, Morrison WH, et al.

Published: 2026-Nov-05

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perineural spread (PNS) in head and neck cancer (HNC) is technically challenging due to complex target volumes adjacent to critical organs. Data on stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for PNS is scarce. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients treated with SBRT for PNS across two centers in the USA and Canada from 2015 to 2025. Endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), local control (LC), and treatment-related toxicity. RESULTS: Thirty-six patients were included, with median follow up of 47.5 months. Two-year OS, PFS, and LC were 79%, 54%, and 72% respectively. Patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) had superior PFS and LC compared with non-cSCC histologies. Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) accounted for the only in-field failures. Grade ≥ 3 toxicity occurred in 22% (8/36), including grade ≥ 3 osteoradionecrosis in 6% (2/36). Temporal lobe necrosis was solely Grade 1-2 (32%). CONCLUSIONS: SBRT demonstrated durable LC for selected patients with PNS, particularly cSCC, while ACC may warrant a dose-escalated approach.

item.title: Outcomes Following Extreme Elective Nodal De-Escalation in HNSCC Treated With Curative Intent: A Community Program Experience.
item.dc:creator: Katzenberg AM, Hockstein L, Ross C, Hanlon AL, Lozano AJ, Ji W, Park S, Clements LI, De Souza-Lawrence LM, Amin JD, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Katzenberg AM, Hockstein L, Ross C, Hanlon AL, Lozano AJ, Ji W, Park S, Clements LI, De Souza-Lawrence LM, Amin JD, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70531
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42984294



Abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE(S): To evaluate elective nodal recurrence rates in HNSCC patients treated with extreme dose de-escalation to 30 or 40 Gy followed by a sequential boost to gross disease or high-risk sites. MATERIALS/METHODS: Between May 2017 and May 2025, patients diagnosed with SCC of the oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx were treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or surgery followed by adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy. Elective nodal volumes (ENV) defined as any uninvolved adjacent, distant ipsilateral or contralateral anatomic nodal level were treated to either 30 or 40 Gy, followed by a sequential boost to the PTVp/PTVn+ or high-risk surgical bed (PTVp+ PTVn+). A subset of 6 patients received 24-36 Gy (1.5-1.8 Gy BID) based on the Mayo-DART regimen. Assignment to 40 Gy versus 30 Gy reflected the radiation oncologist preference based on emerging trial evidence. All cases were reviewed prospectively in a head and neck multidisciplinary conference, and treatment planning required diagnostic FDG PET-CT fused to the planning CT. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 99% of patients. The primary endpoint was regional failure rate within the de-escalated ENV. Secondary endpoints included 1- and 2-year locoregional control (LRC), progression-free survival (PFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), and failure patterns. RESULTS: The analysis included 102 patients of whom the majority 81.4% received definitive chemoradiotherapy, 17.6% underwent surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and 1% received surgery with adjuvant radiation alone. The elective nodal volume was treated to 40 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 81 patients and to 30 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 15 patients; the remaining 6 adjuvant patients received 24-36 Gy at 1.5-1.8 Gy twice daily per the Mayo-DART regimen. With a median follow-up of 26.4 months, no elective nodal failures were observed in either dose cohort. The 1- and 2-year LRC rates were 93.5%. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 88.6% and 87.3%, respectively, while distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) rates were 95.0% and 95.0%, respectively. In total, 13 recurrences were recorded comprising 7 locoregional and 6 distant failures. CONCLUSION: This represents the largest report demonstrating the efficacy of extreme dose de-escalation to ENV's for HNSCC within an NCI designated community cancer program. Reduced doses to the ENV ranging from 40 Gy to as low as 30 Gy were associated with exceptionally low failure rates regardless of treatment approach, stage, or HPV, and validate similar findings previously reported from larger academic centers. Importantly, 99% of patients received concurrent systemic therapy, and these results should not be extrapolated to radiotherapy alone.

item.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
item.dc:creator: Han Y, Yi X, Xia J, Zhang W, Zhao Z, Zhu N, Liu N, Chen X, Wang Y, Feng L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Han Y, Yi X, Xia J, Zhang W, Zhao Z, Zhu N, Liu N, Chen X, Wang Y, Feng L, et al.
Journal: BMJ (Clinical research ed.) | DOI: 10.1136/bmj-2026-101019
Published: 2026-Nov-04

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy. DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial. SETTING: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24. PARTICIPANTS: 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Abstract:
PURPOSE: To refine the suboptimal prognostic discrimination of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th edition TNM (TNM-8) staging system for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with MTC from 43 centers across 15 countries under the framework of the International Medullary Thyroid Cancer Staging Consortium (IMTCSC). Pooled data were analyzed with disease-specific survival as the primary end point. With M1 disease fixed in stage IVC, we redefined the schema for stages I to IVB in M0 patients. Using exhaustive enumeration, all possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion (AIC) defining the proposed system. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and the concordance index (C-index). RESULTS: The IMTCSC cohort included 2,573 patients with MTC (female-to-male ratio: 1.25; median age 52 years [IQR, 41-62]; median follow-up 76.3 months [IQR, 37.3-121.0]). Level VII metastasis correlated with poorer survival, supporting its upgrade to N1c. Exhaustive search of 116,284 admissible stage-grouping schemas identified the optimal model (lowest AIC) defining stages I to IVB: I (T1N0-N1a/T2N0), II (T1N1b/T2N1a/T3N0), III (T1N1c/T2N1b/T3N1a/T4aN0-N1a), IVA (T2N1c/T3N1b-N1c/T4aN1b), and IVB (T4aN1c/T4b any N). Compared with AJCC TNM-8 (stage I as reference; stage II aHR, 0.84, P = .652; stage III aHR, 1.48, P = .172; stage IV aHR, 7.95, P < .001), the proposed system showed a clearer monotonic increase in disease-specific death risk (stage II aHR 2.22; stage III aHR, 4.81; stage IV aHR 15.75; all P ≤ .001) and a higher C-index (0.892 v 0.856, P < .001), which was also evaluated in the SEER cohort (N = 1,909). CONCLUSION: The proposed MTC staging system confers an improved schema for prognostic stratification compared with AJCC TNM-8.

item.title: Impact of Zinc Supplementation and Topical Clobetasol on the Prevention of Regorafenib-Induced Hand-Foot Skin Reaction: The ZINCLO-HAND Study.

Published: 2026-Nov-04

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Regorafenib-induced hand-foot skin reaction (HFSR) is a common dose-limiting toxicity. We evaluated whether prophylaxis with oral zinc plus topical clobetasol is associated with lower clinically significant HFSR compared with either strategy alone. METHODS: ZINCLO-HAND was a prospective, multicenter, pragmatic, nonrandomized comparative study across 13 oncology centers in Türkiye. Adults initiating regorafenib were managed at physician discretion with oral zinc, topical clobetasol propionate 0.05%, or the combination for 8 weeks. The primary end point was grade ≥2 HFSR within the prophylaxis period. Secondary end points included grade 3 HFSR, treatment modification, relative dose intensity, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: Of 179 enrolled patients, 156 were evaluable: zinc, n = 49; clobetasol, n = 52; combination, n = 55. Grade ≥2 HFSR occurred in 38.8%, 38.5%, and 16.4% of patients, respectively (P = .016). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, tumor type, and initial regorafenib dose intensity, zinc monotherapy (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 3.37 [95% CI, 1.30 to 8.71]; P = .012) and clobetasol monotherapy (adjusted OR, 3.15 [95% CI, 1.26 to 7.88]; P = .014) were associated with higher odds of grade ≥2 HFSR versus combination prophylaxis. CONCLUSION: In this nonrandomized prospective cohort, zinc plus topical clobetasol was associated with lower clinically significant regorafenib-induced HFSR and fewer HFSR-attributable treatment modifications. These findings support consideration of combination prophylaxis in routine practice and warrant randomized confirmation.

item.title: Effectiveness of ultraviolet-C robots in isolation room disinfection: Impact of dose, distance, and direct exposure on environmental surface decontamination.
item.dc:creator: Chen YC, Liao WL, Wang SC, Tai CH
item.description:
Authors: Chen YC, Liao WL, Wang SC, Tai CH
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359955
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42981285



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To minimize environmental services staff's exposure to pathogens, ultraviolet-C (UV-C) disinfection robots were applied before terminal manual environmental disinfection. This study aimed to evaluate the disinfection efficacy of the UV-C robot and to assess the effects of ultraviolet-C dose, distance, and direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) on disinfection outcomes. METHODS: This before-after study was conducted in a negative-pressure isolation ward comprising 17 single-patient rooms at a medical center in Taiwan between August 24, 2024, and January 3, 2025, yielding a total of 270 paired samples. An ultraviolet-C-emitting robot with a wavelength of 254 nm was sequentially positioned on both sides of the patient bed and operated for 5 minutes on each side before routine manual environmental disinfection. Total aerobic colony counts (ACC) and bacterial culture positivity rates were obtained from high-touch environmental surfaces (e.g., bed rails, call bells and bedside chairs) before and after UV-C disinfection. The effects of UV-C dose, distance between the robot and surfaces, and the presence of direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) versus indirect exposure on disinfection efficacy were analyzed using multivariate binary logistic regression, performed using SPSS version 27.0. The results of the regression analysis were expressed as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The median ACC and bacterial culture positivity rates on surfaces significantly decreased after UV-C disinfection (0.76 vs. 0.08 CFU/cm²; 83% vs. 57.4%, P < 0.001). A weak negative correlation was observed between ACC and UV-C doses after disinfection (rs = -0.281, 95% CI: -0.390 to -0.164, P < 0.001), while no correlation (rs = 0.040, 95% CI: -0.083 to 0.162, P = 0.510) and weak correlation (rs = 0.317, 95% CI: 0.202 to 0.424, P <  0.001) were found between ACC at short and long irradiation distances. The ACC on environmental surfaces with direct UV-C exposure were significantly lower than those in shadowed areas [median: 0.00 (IQR: 0.00 to 0.44) vs. median: 0.16 (IQR: 0.00 to 0.80); P < 0.001]. Multivariate logistic regression identified direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) as the strongest predictor of negative bacterial culture results, reducing the odds of bacterial culture positivity by 79.5% compared to indirect exposure (OR = 0.205, 95% CI: 0.083 to 0.508, P < 0.001) in the layout of the negative pressure isolation room in this study. CONCLUSIONS: Ultraviolet-C robots serve as an effective disinfection intervention for hospital environments. Their efficacy is most pronounced when direct exposure (line-of-sight irradiation) is achieved in the isolation rooms. Therefore, aligning movable items toward the UV-C robot prior to disinfection, alongside subsequent manual environmental disinfection and physical debris removal, remains essential, particularly in shadowed areas.

item.title: Explainable computational framework for subtype classification and biomarker identification in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning.
item.dc:creator: Rajan A, Biji CL, Sinha MG, Oviya IR
item.description:
Authors: Rajan A, Biji CL, Sinha MG, Oviya IR
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360612
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42981280



Abstract:
The precise classification of basal, classical, atypical, and mesenchymal subtypes of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is crucial for advancing precision oncology. Our research aims to develop an explainable subtype classification model for HNSCC.These molecular subtypes have been previously defined; reliable and meaningful computational methods for the classification of molecular subtypes and prioritization of molecular biomarkers for each subtype do not exist. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies molecular subtypes based on combined transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA-HNSC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE65858). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify the importance of genes for model predictions. Subsequently, genes with high predictive importance were analyzed in protein-protein interactions using STRING, and hub genes were identified by Maximum Clique Centrality (MCC) and used for the identification of candidate biomarkers for each of the subtypes. We employed machine learning methods such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost (AB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), XGBoost (XGB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). The XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 95% after hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. Biologically relevant subtype-specific biomarkers associated with each molecular subtype were identified. To highlight the potential biological functions of these biomarkers, pathway analysis was performed. Further assessment of these genes, such as survival analysis and druggability, showed promise for the development of targeted therapies.

item.title: Symptom trajectories in head and neck cancer from diagnosis to long-term survivorship.
item.dc:creator: Fenech AL, Park ER, Wirth LJ, D'Souza G, Humphris G, Siegel SD, Pring M, Laurenceau JP
item.description:
Authors: Fenech AL, Park ER, Wirth LJ, D'Souza G, Humphris G, Siegel SD, Pring M, Laurenceau JP
Journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice | DOI: 10.1007/s11764-026-02146-7
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 42980934



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) experience substantial symptom burden related to both disease and intensive treatments. Understanding long-term symptom patterns may help identify patients at risk for persistent emotional and physical symptom burden. This study evaluated symptom trajectories of anxiety, depression, fear of cancer recurrence (FCR), and oral pain among patients with HNC from diagnosis through long-term survivorship. METHODS: This secondary analysis included 5411 patients with HNC from the Head and Neck 5000 study in the UK. Latent class growth analysis (LCGA) and growth mixture modeling (GMM) were used to examine changes in symptoms, predictors of class membership, and within-class variability. RESULTS: The majority of patients were classified into a mild symptom class for depression (58%), anxiety (48%), and oral pain (62%), whereas the largest FCR class (44%) represented moderate symptoms. Anxiety, FCR, and oral pain followed recovery trajectories characterized by symptom improvement, while depression demonstrated a distinct pattern of worsening symptoms. Across symptoms, nearly 20% of patients belonged to an elevated symptom trajectory. These patients were more likely to be younger in age, have lower income, and report greater weekly alcohol consumption. Patients with HPV-positive HNC experienced faster reductions in anxiety and FCR but greater increases in depression over time. CONCLUSIONS: Distinct symptom trajectories were observed into long-term survivorship among patients with HNC. Although most patients experienced mild-to-moderate symptoms, a clinically important subgroup remained at elevated risk for persistent symptoms. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Early identification of patients at risk for persistent symptoms may facilitate targeted supportive care and behavioral interventions to improve long-term survivorship outcomes.

item.title: Impact of Body Mass Index on Treatment Outcomes in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer Patients Treated With Definitive Chemoradiotherapy or Radiotherapy Alone.
