item.description:
Authors: Pandey A, Pandey L, Mishra V, Singh P, Kunduru HPR, Lohia S, Pasricha R, Pasricha Y
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70537
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 42980345



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a readily measured indicator of nutritional status; however, its impact on outcomes in head and neck cancer (HNC) patients remains understudied. This study evaluated the impact of pre-treatment BMI on toxicities and survival in such patients. METHODS: This retrospective study included 212 patients of locally advanced HNC treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone. Patients were categorized into BMI < 25 kg/m2 and ≥ 25 kg/m2. Toxicities were assessed using CTCAE v5.0. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional control (LRC) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Eighty-six percent of patients had BMI of < 25Kg/m2. These patients experienced significantly higher rates of grade ≥ 2 mucositis, dermatitis, candidiasis, and greater need for nutritional support (44.7%; p = 0.039). Median OS and LRC were 25 and 24 months, respectively. Three-year OS and LRC were 46.3% and 39%. BMI category, T stage, and nodal stage independently predicted OS. CONCLUSION: BMI < 25 Kg/m2 patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone are more prone to treatment-related toxicities and have inferior survival outcomes. Early nutritional assessment and intervention should be integrated into routine management to improve treatment outcomes.

item.title: Does Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Increase Reconstructive Risk? A Comparative Analysis of Surgical Efficiency and Microvascular Success in Advanced OSCC.
item.dc:creator: Najjar E, Abdelraziq M, Yaniv D, Ritter A, Abu-Elnaaj I, Ghantous Y
item.description:
Authors: Najjar E, Abdelraziq M, Yaniv D, Ritter A, Abu-Elnaaj I, Ghantous Y
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70534
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 42979766



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) by evaluating its impact on surgical efficiency and postoperative morbidity in patients undergoing complex free-flap reconstruction for advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). METHODS: A retrospective comparative study was conducted on 86 patients (NACT cohort: n = 20; Primary Surgery cohort: n = 66) undergoing microvascular free tissue transfer. Primary outcomes included surgical efficiency (ischemic time, total operative duration) and postoperative complications (major microvascular events vs. minor wound issues) that were evaluated. RESULTS: The NACT group presented with significantly more advanced disease (100% Stage IV vs. 39.4%; p < 0.001). Despite this higher tumor burden, the NACT cohort demonstrated significantly shorter mean ischemic times (39.0 ± 7.5 vs. 52.5 ± 17.9 min; p = 0.001) and reduced operative durations (7.5 ± 0.8 vs. 8.6 ± 1.3 h; p = 0.001). Total complication rates were comparable (35% vs. 33.3%). However, minor wound-related complications were significantly more frequent in the NACT group (30% vs. 4.5%; p = 0.004). The flap salvage rate following re-exploration was high and comparable between groups (80.0% vs. 85.7%). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were detected in major flap failure or vascular re-exploration, though the study was underpowered to establish definitive safety equivalence for these endpoints. In exploratory subgroup analysis of RFFF reconstructions, NACT was associated with reduced ischemic time (p = 0.017). These findings suggest that while NACT compromises soft-tissue wound healing, it does not preclude successful microvascular reconstruction when managed with appropriate perioperative care.

item.title: An Update of Management Strategies in Locally Advanced Oral Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Singh A, Chaturvedi P
item.description:
Authors: Singh A, Chaturvedi P
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70534
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 42979722



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains surgically anchored, but systemic treatment is evolving rapidly, particularly with perioperative immunotherapy. METHODS: We reviewed clinical evidence on neoadjuvant, adjuvant, maintenance, and altered-dose systemic strategies for resectable locally advanced OSCC and relevant head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. RESULTS: Conventional neoadjuvant chemotherapy has not improved survival in unselected resectable OSCC and should be reserved for selected indications including borderline resectability, mandibular preservation, and conversion to surgery. Neoadjuvant immunotherapy studies using PD-1 blockade, dual checkpoint inhibition, chemoimmunotherapy, targeted-immunotherapy combinations, and SBRT-immunotherapy have demonstrated feasible delivery and meaningful pathological responses. KEYNOTE-689 established improved event-free survival with perioperative pembrolizumab. Postoperatively, cisplatin-radiotherapy remains standard for positive margins and extranodal extension, while NIVOPOST-OP supports nivolumab intensification in high-risk disease. Maintenance therapy remains uncertain, with negative MACE results but a possible benefit from tegafur-uracil in selected patients. CONCLUSION: Perioperative immunotherapy is reshaping resectable OSCC treatment. Postoperative intensification, maintenance therapy, and lower-dose strategies, including low-dose nivolumab with metronomic therapy, require prospective validation. These approaches may be especially important in resource-constrained settings, where treatment cost and access remain major barriers.

item.title: Living longer or living better - priorities among head and neck cancer survivors.
item.dc:creator: Thomsen A, Trigui N, Rast J, Newton-Tanzer E, Donate MG, Hoffmann M, Wiegand S
item.description:
Authors: Thomsen A, Trigui N, Rast J, Newton-Tanzer E, Donate MG, Hoffmann M, Wiegand S
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-17298-z
Published: 2026-Nov-03
PMID: 42977905



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck cancer and its treatment can profoundly affect physical function, psychosocial well-being, and overall quality of life (QoL). As survival rates improve, integrating patient-reported outcomes and individual treatment preferences into clinical decision-making has become increasingly important. This study aimed to assess the preferences of head and neck cancer (HNC) survivors regarding QoL versus life prolongation in order to better inform patient-centered treatment decisions. METHODS: Adult head and neck cancer survivors completed validated questionnaires assessing health-related QoL (EORTC QLQ-C30), distress (Distress Thermometer), and preferences for QoL versus life prolongation (QQ questionnaire). Multivariable regression analyses were used to identify predictors of QoL and distress, while associations between patient characteristics and treatment preference were examined using group comparisons. RESULTS: The study included 207 patients (70.5% male; mean age 66.2 years). The median global health status (QLQ-C30) was 66.6, and the median distress score was 3, indicating a relatively good overall QoL and a comparatively low level of psychological distress. In multivariable analysis, lower distress and employment (both p < 0.001) as well as surgical treatment and lower comorbidity (both p < 0.05) were independently associated with better QoL. Independent predictors of distress included sex, global health status, tumor stage, educational level, and treatment modality (all p < 0.05). Regarding preferences (n = 202), 53.0% of patients prioritized QoL, 21.8% favored life prolongation, and 25.2% reported no clear preference. Preference was significantly associated with age (p = 0.035), with older patients favoring QoL, and with tumor stage (p = 0.032), with the differences between options diminishing in advanced stages. CONCLUSION: QoL in head and neck cancer survivors is shaped by both clinical and psychosocial factors. Lower distress, employment, surgical treatment, and lower comorbidity were associated with better QoL, while most patients prioritized QoL over life prolongation, particularly at older age. These findings emphasize the need to align treatment strategies with patient values, placing QoL at the center of clinical decision-making.

item.title: Assessing Predictive Utility of Ultrasound for Tumor Characteristics in Thyroid Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Jacob T, Hayat L, Krutik D, Kotz L, Carmel-Neidermann NN, Shendler G, Izkhakov E, Pestrikov T, Trejo L, Muhanna N, et al.
item.description:

Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71020
Published: 2026-Nov-03

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the accuracy of preoperative ultrasound in estimating tumor size, multifocality, and extrathyroidal extension in papillary thyroid carcinoma. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center, including patients who underwent curative surgery for papillary thyroid carcinoma between 2006 and 2022. Agreement between preoperative ultrasound-estimated and postoperative pathologic tumor size was assessed overall and across predefined size categories (≤ 1 cm, 1-2 cm, 2-3 cm, 3-4 cm, and > 4 cm). The diagnostic performance of ultrasound for detecting multifocality and extrathyroidal extension was also evaluated. RESULTS: The medical records of a total of 931 patients were reviewed. The mean sonographic and pathologic tumor sizes were 2.10 ± 1.42 cm and 1.64 ± 1.28 cm, respectively (p < 0.001). Ultrasound consistently overestimated tumor size across all groups, with the mean percentage difference rising from 6% in tumors ≤ 1 cm to 32% in tumors > 4 cm (p < 0.001). The overall mean percent difference was +15.7 ± 40.7%, indicating bias toward larger sonographic measurements. Ultrasound detection of extrathyroidal extension showed a positive predictive value of 30% and a negative predictive value of 95%; a positive predictive value of 40% and a negative predictive value of 85% for multifocality. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that ultrasound tends to overestimate tumor size and that it has limited predictive accuracy for multifocality and extrathyroidal extension. They demonstrate the need for caution when planning a total thyroidectomy based solely upon preoperative ultrasound findings in the absence of suspected nodal metastasis.

item.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial.

Abstract:
Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. item.title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women.
item.dc:creator: Chen C, Hao L, Xie W, Tang R, Guo R, Zhang Z, Li J, Liang D, Jin M, Zheng Z, et al.

Abstract:
Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. Vaginocervical and urinary niches showed the most pronounced restructuring, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. MHT efficacy also varied according to baseline gut community type: Phocaeicola vulgatus-dominated women exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness, superior clinical outcomes and were more likely to achieve 4-week rapid clinical remission than Prevotella copri-dominated women. Abstract:

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) with taxane, platinum, and cetuximab (TPC) prior to surgical resection of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) can result in dramatic decreases in tumor burden in critical anatomic subsites. We investigate the impact of TPC-based NACT on surgical morbidity and compare oncologic outcomes to a propensity-matched conventionally treated cohort. METHODS: Between 2015 and 2023, 44 patients who received TPC prior to definitive surgical resection of OCSCC were identified. Charts were retrospectively reviewed to classify the extent of resection proposed at initial presentation versus the completed surgery after NACT. Patients were classified as having undergone response-adapted surgery (RAS), standard surgery (SS), or extended surgery (ES). Surgical morbidity was quantified using a Surgical Morbidity scoring system. Oncological outcomes were compared to a propensity score-matched cohort treated with upfront primary surgery, matched on age, sex, WUHNCI, clinical T status, clinical N status and oral cavity subsite. RESULTS: Of 44 patients, 20 underwent RAS, 21 had SS, and 3 required ES. RAS patients had less extensive operations and decreased morbidity: 12 total or subtotal glossectomies were reduced to hemi- or partial glossectomies, 9 cheek flaps and 5 mandibulotomies were avoided, and 2 segmental mandibulectomies were converted to marginal mandibulectomies. Four received fasciocutaneous rather than osteocutaneous free flaps, and 2 no longer required a free flap. A trend toward improved 2-year DSS in the RAS versus SS group did not reach significance (p = 0.089). TPC NACT patients had improved 5-year overall survival compared with propensity-matched controls (73 % vs. 40 %, p = 0.003). Disease-specific survival was also higher in the NACT cohort (75 % vs. 49 %, p = 0.013). There were trends toward improved local and regional recurrence-free probability in the NACT cohort, though neither reached statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: TPC NACT prior to definitive surgery for OCSCC was associated with reduced surgical morbidity. RAS patients underwent less morbid surgeries while maintaining comparable survival. There was no detrimental impact on survival in NACT patients compared to matched non-NACT patients.

item.title: Spreading the Joy of Literacy: A community-based survey of parents by parents.
item.dc:creator: Collins-McGowan S, Aligne CA, McDermott K, Cabral C, Ramos Benitez AP, Lomack M, Mayo N
item.description:
Authors: Collins-McGowan S, Aligne CA, McDermott K, Cabral C, Ramos Benitez AP, Lomack M, Mayo N
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361893
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Literacy is an important social determinant of health. Failure to develop emergent literacy skills before kindergarten is a risk factor for academic failure, poverty, incarceration, and early death. Reading comprehension depends on both language comprehension and alphabetic decoding skills. The Home Literacy Environment literature tends to focus on reading aloud to develop oral language but less is known about letter-themed tools. DESIGN: Our hypothesis was that letter-themed toys and books would be acceptable to all families but that lower socio-economic status (SES) households would be less likely to have them. Using methods of Community Based Participatory Research, 3 caregivers with young children living in the City of Rochester, NY, completed IRB training and provided cultural context for decisions throughout this study. We surveyed a convenience sample of 156 caregivers at 10 community events. We showed a poster with pictures of alphabet-themed toys and asked caregivers to count how many they had in the home. ZIP code was used as a proxy for SES. RESULTS: We surveyed 156 caregivers, excluding 13 responses because of missing information. Of the 143 remaining, 139 (97.2%) thought it was important that a child know most of the alphabet letters before kindergarten. 1 in 4 of our respondents didn't have a single literacy toy in their home and an additional 1 in 6 had only one. We calculated a p value of 0.0004 for the hypothesis that there is a difference by SES in the number of these items in the home. CONCLUSIONS: Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that joyful letter-themed tools are acceptable to parents in general but that low-SES households are less likely to have them. item.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial.

Abstract:

Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although a rare malignancy, anal cancer incidence is increasing with a growing proportion diagnosed at advanced stages. Our objective was to evaluate factors associated with advanced stage-at-diagnosis (stage 3+) of squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (SCCA) among men and women with and without HIV. METHODS: We analyzed U.S. National Cancer Database data (2004-2020) for patients aged 18-89 years with SCCA (ICD-O-3: C210-C218). The outcome was advanced stage at diagnosis (stage 3/4). Stratified by sex, we assessed associations with demographics, HIV status, healthcare access (facility type, insurance), and geographic factors using hierarchical multivariable Poisson regression to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Among 36,389 patients with SCCA, 2,600 (7.1%) were living with HIV and 42% were diagnosed at stage 3-4. Women without HIV were more likely to be diagnosed at an advanced stage compared to men without HIV (aPR: 1.20, 95% CI: 1.05-1.37). item.title: The Effects of Radioiodine Treatment on Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients Treated for a Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Bondet de La Bernardie S, Lussey-Lepoutre C, Buffet C, Bernier MO, Singer S, Baudin C
item.description:
Authors: Bondet de La Bernardie S, Lussey-Lepoutre C, Buffet C, Bernier MO, Singer S, Baudin C
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261499230
Published: 2026-Nov-03
PMID: 42975204



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) has markedly increased since the 1990s. The patients' health-related quality of life (HRQoL) is an essential outcome to consider, both short- and long-term. After thyroidectomy, treatment generally includes radioiodine therapy (RIT), the impact of which on HRQoL remains debated, particularly in patients at low risk of recurrence. This systematic review with meta-analysis aims to comprehensively evaluate the association of RIT with HRQoL in patients with DTC throughout the disease trajectory. METHODS: A systematic literature review was conducted, and the findings are reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies published between January 2000 and June 2026. Observational studies and randomized controlled trials assessing HRQoL in patients with DTC treated with RIT were eligible for inclusion. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomized trials. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed when the data allowed. RESULTS: In total, 53 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 6 were included in the meta-analyses. Before the administration of RIT, patients' HRQoL was already impaired compared with that of the general population. After RIT, the onset of certain symptoms had sometimes a negative impact on HRQoL. Few months post treatment, an overall improvement in HRQoL was observed in most patients compared with baseline. More than one year post treatment, HRQoL approach is that of the general population. CONCLUSIONS: Symptoms or anxiety associated with RIT may impair HRQoL around the time of treatment. HRQoL tends to approach that of the general population, although it does not consistently reach the same level. Furthermore, some patients may continue to experience persistent symptoms whose severity depends on the dose received. The heterogeneity of the results highlights the importance of future studies using more homogeneous and thyroid-specific questionnaires, and to include analyses adjusted for confounding factors such as administered activity and preparation methods, along with a pre-surgical assessment, in order to better evaluate the specific effect of RIT on HRQoL.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accurate evaluation of glottic anatomy in adults with dysphonia can be challenging when videostroboscopy is limited by altered anatomy, supraglottic hyperfunction, or posterior glottic pathology. We sought to evaluate the clinical utility of Dynamic Voice Computed Tomography (DVCT) in complex adult voice patients with prior laryngeal framework surgery or suspected posterior glottic insufficiency (PGI). METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 15 adult patients undergoing DVCT for evaluation of dysphonia at a tertiary laryngology practice between February 2025 and February 2026. Demographics, prior surgical history, standardized voice measures, videostroboscopy findings. RESULTS: Fifteen adults underwent DVCT (mean age 62.8 years; 40% female). Ten had prior thyroplasty, and five had known or suspected PGI. All had abnormal acoustic and perceptual voice measures out of proportion to stroboscopy appearance. DVCT imaging findings and clinical management were analyzed. DVCT provided additional clinically relevant anatomic information beyond videostroboscopy in all patients. Imaging most commonly identified posterior glottic insufficiency, vertical height mismatch, implant malposition, or arytenoid malposition not fully appreciated on stroboscopy. CT findings influenced surgical decision-making in the majority of patients, confirming candidacy in 47%, altering planned procedures in 33%, and avoiding surgery in 13%. CONCLUSIONS: DVCT is a useful tool in the evaluation of dysphonic adults with prior laryngeal framework surgery or PGI, providing complementary characterization of glottic anatomy that informs surgical decision making.

item.title: Expression of nestin in cancer: a tissue microarray study involving 13,318 cancers from 148 tumor entities.
item.dc:creator: Schraps N, Torzewski M, von Bargen C, Gehrisch F, Menz A, Lutz F, Chirico V, Viehweger F, Dum D, Schlichter R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Schraps N, Torzewski M, von Bargen C, Gehrisch F, Menz A, Lutz F, Chirico V, Viehweger F, Dum D, Schlichter R, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-17190-w
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42972270



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nestin (neuroepithelial stem cell protein) is a class VI intermediate filament protein which is transiently expressed in subsets of precursor cells of various tissues during development. Nestin expression can be reinduced in the adult during pathological situations. METHODS: To better comprehend the prevalence of nestin in different cancer types, nestin was analyzed by immunohistochemistry on tissue microarrays (TMAs) containing 17,285 samples from 148 different tumor types. Our antibody was validated using a second independent antibody on 76 different normal tissues, ensuring a broad range of proteins to be tested for cross-reactivity. RESULTS: Of 13,318 analyzable tumors, nestin staining was absent in 11,677 (87.7%), weak in 961 (7.2%), moderate in 360 (2.7%), and strong in 320 (2.4%) cases. Of 148 tumor categories, 119 showed nestin staining in at least one case, and 57 included at least one sample with strong positivity. Nestin positivity was most seen in tumors of the salivary glands (up to 100%), gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (93.8%), tumors of the peripheral nerves (up to 93.8%) and malignant melanomas (81.8%). High nestin expression was linked to high grade (p < 0.0001), estrogen (p = 0.0054), and progesterone receptor negativity (p = 0.0051), as well as a triple negative phenotype (p = 0.0028) in invasive breast cancer NST, in papillary as well as poor ISUP (p=0.0149), Fuhrman (p=0.0006) and Thoenes grades (p=0.0099) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, invasive tumor growth in urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (pTa vs. pT2-4; p < 0.0001), and advanced pT stage (p = 0.0477) in serous carcinoma of the ovary. CONCLUSIONS: The data from this study provide an overview of nestin expression in human cancer and demonstrate that increased nestin levels can occur in many different tumor entities. Significant associations with unfavorable tumor characteristics in multiple entities argue for a role of nestin in driving cancer aggressiveness, which may further support the concept of exploring nestin as a drug target.

item.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Nov-02

Abstract:
There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. item.title: Efficacy of Intratympanic Sodium Thiosulfate Gel Injection to Prevent Cisplatin-Induced Ototoxicity.

item.description:
Authors: Vittayakoonsakulchai K, Pitathawatchai P, Plodpai Y, Atchariyasathian V, Khaimook W, Kirtsreesakul V, Kittichet R, Prayuenyong P
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71028
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42971568



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intratympanic sodium thiosulfate (STS) gel injection in preventing cisplatin-induced hearing loss. METHODS: We conducted a single-blinded randomized controlled trial, enrolling adults with head and neck cancer undergoing cisplatin chemotherapy. Intratympanic STS gel was injected into one ear within 3 h before each cisplatin cycle, while the contralateral ear served as a control. Clinical and audiometric assessments were performed before each injection and 1-3 months after the completion of chemotherapy. Changes in hearing thresholds from baseline at each frequency were measured. Ototoxicity was defined according to the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA) criteria. Adverse events associated with intratympanic STS gel injections were also monitored. RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were included in the study. Based on ASHA criteria within the frequency range of 0.25-8 kHz, there was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of ototoxicity between the treated and control ears (p = 0.683). Compared with control ears, treated ears exhibited significantly reduced threshold shifts from baseline in the 4, 6, 8, 9, and 11 kHz, with mean differences of approximately 7-10 dB. Nonetheless, intratympanic STS gel injections demonstrated potential benefits in preserving hearing at high and extended-high frequencies. The procedure was generally well-tolerated, with manageable adverse effects. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Androgen Receptor-Targeted Therapy for Salivary Gland Carcinoma: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Rosenthal JW, Allen DZ, Sternthal J, Romeo I, Ari G, Brammer B, Reardon EE, Novaes JAMO, Saba NF, Gross J, et al.

Published: 2026-Nov-02

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Salivary duct carcinoma (SDC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with limited effective treatment options in the recurrent/metastatic setting. Biologically, SDC has high rates of androgen receptor (AR) expression, providing a strong rationale for AR-targeted therapy. DATA SOURCES: Ovid MEDLINE, Embase.com, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov from their inception to August 20, 2026. REVIEW METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of AR-targeted therapy in patients with AR-positive recurrent/metastatic SDC and SDC-enriched salivary gland carcinoma cohorts. The primary outcome was overall response rate (ORR). Secondary outcomes included clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Pooled proportions were calculated using a random-effects model. Combined androgen blockade was compared to AR-targeted monotherapy. RESULTS: Twelve studies were included in the systematic review accounting for 587 eligible patients. The primary meta-analysis has 10 eligible studies (417 patients). The pooled ORR was 26.6% (95% CI, 15.4%-42.1%). Five studies reported CBR, and the pooled CBR was 45.0% (95% CI, 38.1%-52.1%). The sample-size-weighted mean of reported median PFS was 6.3 months, and the weighted mean of reported median OS was 26.9 months among the seven studies reporting OS. ORR was higher with combined androgen blockade than with AR-targeted monotherapy (36.3% vs. 8.9%; meta-regression p = 0.023). CONCLUSION: AR-targeted therapy shows clinically meaningful activity in AR-positive disease, particularly with combined androgen blockade. The evidence remains heterogeneous and largely nonrandomized, so treatment decisions should account for HER2 status, AR expression level, treatment line, and patient tolerance.

item.title: Primary carcinoma of the lacrimal drainage system: a systematic review of treatment, outcomes and associated prognostic factors.
item.dc:creator: Bertolini M, Conti C, Caviglia A, Moro C, Fucci L, Rossi M, Iandelli A, Peretti G, Mauritz Canevari FR
item.description:
Authors: Bertolini M, Conti C, Caviglia A, Moro C, Fucci L, Rossi M, Iandelli A, Peretti G, Mauritz Canevari FR
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108198
Published: 2026-Nov-02

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary carcinoma of the lacrimal drainage system (NLCA) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with poorly defined prognostic factors and no established treatment guidelines. OBJECTIVE: To characterize epidemiological and histopathological features, evaluate survival outcomes, and identify independent prognostic factors through a pooled analysis. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted per PRISMA guidelines. Individual patient-level data were pooled for logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. A random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was performed on aggregate data from retrospective case series. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI Critical Appraisal Checklists. RESULTS: Eighty-one studies encompassing 201 patients were included. The most frequent histologic subtype was squamous cell carcinoma (38.3 %), followed by adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC, 15.4 %). Estimated 2-year overall survival, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and metastasis-free survival (MFS) were 96 %, 88 %, and 92 %; 5-year RFS and MFS were 85 % and 91 %. ACC was independently associated with disease-related death (OR 1.79, 95 % CI 1.04-3.09, p = 0.037) and with significantly worse overall survival (log-rank p = 0.013). Positive surgical margins (R1) were associated with higher odds of recurrence (OR 8.68, 95 % CI 1.99-37.81, p = 0.004), metastasis (OR 5.05, 95 % CI 1.02-25.04, p = 0.048), and death (OR 9.62, 95 % CI 1.10-83.89, p = 0.040). Pooled recurrence, metastasis, and mortality rates were 15.0 %, 13.5 %, and 13.3 %, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, positive surgical margins and ACC histology were associated with worse oncological outcomes. Given the primary independent prognostic determinants in NLCA, R0 resection should be the principal surgical objective, while ACC warrants intensified surveillance. Multicentre prospective studies are needed to define optimal treatment algorithms.

item.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. Abstract:
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a re-emerging arbovirus that causes debilitating inflammatory arthritis, for which no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. This study investigated the potential of repurposing erlotinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, as an anti-CHIKV agent. Erlotinib demonstrated promising in vitro antiviral activity, with EC50 values in the low micromolar range and a favorable selectivity index. However, in vivo evaluation in C57BL/6 mice revealed pharmacokinetic limitations, characterized by rapid absorption and clearance, resulting in insufficient drug exposure under standard dosing regimens. Escalation to an intensive four-times-daily (QID) regimen successfully maintained plasma concentrations above the in vitro therapeutic threshold but led to significant body weight loss and failed to reduce viral titers or viral RNA levels in infected tissues. However, a once-daily (OD) regimen improved tolerability and significantly reduced footpad and serum viral titers relative to vehicle-treated controls. Notably, despite the lack of virological control in the QID regimen, erlotinib treatment reduced leukocyte infiltration and tissue inflammation in both treatment regimens, indicating a host-directed immunomodulatory effect. Overall, these findings highlight the critical role of dosing frequency in determining erlotinib's in vivo antiviral efficacy against CHIKV and suggest that once-daily (OD) administration may represent a more viable dosing strategy for further evaluation of erlotinib as a host-directed antiviral against CHIKV. Future strategies should also explore combination approaches with direct-acting antivirals to achieve more viral suppression and mitigation of disease pathology, as well as Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR)-guided scaffold optimization to improve in vivo pharmacokinetic profiles.

item.title: Women's experience following orthodontic treatment with conventional fixed appliances and clear aligners: A qualitative study.
item.dc:creator: San Nicolas Dubrull Lia Lucarelli N, Gonçalves Innocente G, Augusto Thiene Leme P, Paz Sampaio L, Gonzaga Gandini Junior L, Amélia Scudeler Vedovello S, Arrais Campos L, Carmo de Menezes C
item.description:
Authors: San Nicolas Dubrull Lia Lucarelli N, Gonçalves Innocente G, Augusto Thiene Leme P, Paz Sampaio L, Gonzaga Gandini Junior L, Amélia Scudeler Vedovello S, Arrais Campos L, Carmo de Menezes C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359709
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42970542



Abstract:
This qualitative study aimed to explore the experiences of female patients following completion of orthodontic treatment with conventional fixed appliances and clear aligners. It used a clinical qualitative design with, semi-structured interviews featuring open-ended questions. Participants were recruited from private orthodontic practices, and the sample size was determined by data saturation. The final group included six patients treated with conventional fixed appliances and nine patients treated with clear aligners. Data were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with peer validation of the categories. Seven categories emerged among patients treated with conventional fixed appliances: pain, discomfort, and hygiene difficulties; daily adaptations and restrictions; confidence in the professional; treatment duration; insecurity or embarrassment; desire to improve appearance; and satisfaction with treatment outcomes. For patients treated with clear aligners, seven categories were identified: practicality, comfort and hygiene; pain and discomfort related to use; treatment duration; willingness to recommend aligners; desire to improve appearance and appliance discretion; recommendation by the professional; and satisfaction. The findings show that, although patients with fixed appliances faced several challenges during treatment, aesthetic improvement was the main reason for seeking care, and overall satisfaction with the results was high. Patients who chose clear aligners aimed to avoid common limitations of fixed appliances and emphasized benefits related to comfort, convenience, oral hygiene, and discretion. These results highlight the importance of qualitative methods for understanding patient perspectives and can guide clinical communication and shared decision-making in adult orthodontic treatment.

item.title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship.
item.dc:creator: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL
item.description:
Authors: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361602
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42970519



Abstract:
Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

item.title: Opium Consumption and Lung Cancer: From Self-reported Use to Exposure Biomarkers.
item.dc:creator: Leng S
item.description:
Authors: Leng S
Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology | DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-26-1173
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42968657



Abstract:
Opium consumption is most prevalent in Southwestern and South Asia, particularly in regions surrounding the major opium-producing areas of the Golden Crescent. The International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies opium consumption as a group 1 human carcinogen, with sufficient evidence for lung, laryngeal, and urinary bladder cancers. Opium consumption involves complex exposure profiles, including combustion-derived exposures from opium and its fuels, as well as coexposures from tobacco smoking and indoor biomass burning. Recent molecular epidemiologic research in the prospective Golestan Cohort Study provides an opportunity to move beyond self-reported opium use by characterizing internal exposure to multiple opioid and non-opioid constituents. In a nested case-control study of 53 matched lung cancer pairs among opium users, 35 urinary metabolites reflecting exposure to opiates, volatile organic compounds, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and nicotine were measured. Higher concentrations of morphine-3-glucuronide, morphine-6-glucuronide, 2-hydroxypropyl mercapturic acid, and 2-hydroxyethyl mercapturic acid were associated with lung cancer. These findings provide an important initial demonstration of the potential of urinary biomarkers to characterize complex exposures associated with opium consumption. Future studies integrating driver mutations, mutational signatures, and tumor microenvironment characteristics may provide further insight into mechanisms of opium-related lung carcinogenesis and inform cancer prevention and precision oncology. See related article by Naghash et al., p. 1880.

item.title: Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems Policy Divergence and Surveillance Gaps: A Cancer Prevention Blind Spot in the WHO South-East Asia Region.
item.dc:creator: Pandey S, Pandey M, Aryal B
item.description:
Authors: Pandey S, Pandey M, Aryal B
Journal: JCO global oncology | DOI: 10.1200/GO-25-00630
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42981554



Abstract:
The unregulated proliferation of electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) risks undermining decades of progress in global cancer prevention. Nepal's recent regulatory uncertainty, rooted in a mismatch between primary legislation and subordinate regulation, provides an instructive case for comparative policy analysis across the WHO South-East Asia Region, which already carries a disproportionate oral cancer burden attributable to smokeless tobacco use. Using Nepal, India, and Bangladesh as contrasting policy trajectories, we examine how statutory prohibition, legislative reversal, and contested enforcement intersect with this pre-existing burden. Although ENDS may confer harm reduction benefits among certain adults who smoke, realizing this potential depends on effective product regulation, prevention of youth access, and population-level surveillance; these conditions remain weak or nonexistent in many LMICs. We argue that failure to incorporate ENDS explicitly into primary tobacco control legislation constitutes an actionable governance gap. Explicit legislative coverage of ENDS and harmonization of regional surveillance systems represent minimum safeguards before exposure patterns become entrenched and long-term cancer risks can be reliably assessed.

item.title: Association of HPV Status With Quality of Life After Transoral Robotic Surgery for T1-T2 Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Tesauro P, Khalaf M, Breuskin I, Mercante G, Temam S, Gorphe P
item.description:
Authors: Tesauro P, Khalaf M, Breuskin I, Mercante G, Temam S, Gorphe P
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70540
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42968417



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In T1-T2 oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), factors associated with patient-reported quality of life after transoral robotic surgery (TORS) are poorly defined. METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 59 patients with T1-T2 OPSCC treated with TORS. Swallowing-related quality of life (MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory, MDADI) and EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-H&N35 scores were analyzed with mixed-effects models adjusted for HPV status, subsite, adjuvant treatment and, in sensitivity analyses, lifestyle factors, age, tumor stage, and preoperative scores. RESULTS: HPV-positive status was independently associated with higher MDADI scores (β = 12.39, p = 0.001), including after adjustment for preoperative scores (β = 16.0, p = 0.004), and with lower QLQ-H&N35 symptom burden (β = -9.5, p = 0.012). Adjuvant radiotherapy was associated with lower MDADI scores (β = -7.92, p = 0.021), attenuated after adjustment for tumor stage. Tumor subsite was not associated with outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: HPV-positive patients report better swallowing-related quality of life after TORS, independently of preoperative scores.

item.title: Association between absolute lymphocyte count and outcomes of radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy in elderly patients with inoperable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Y, Chen W, Ni D, Liang X
item.description:
Authors: Jiang Y, Chen W, Ni D, Liang X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1953153
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42997324



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pretreatment absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) is related to clinical outcomes among elderly patients with inoperable ESCC receiving definitive radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy. METHODS: Elderly patients (≥ 60 years) with incurable ESCC who underwent programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor therapy and definitive radiotherapy were retrospectively enrolled. ROC analysis identified the most discriminative ALC cutoff. Short-term efficacy was compared between groups, and Cox regression assessed factors related to overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: Data from 102 elderly patients were evaluated. The objective response rate (ORR) was 70.59%; median PFS and OS were 21 and 28 months, respectively. ROC analysis identified 1.24 × 109/L as the cutoff value for ALC. The response rate was markedly higher among patients with high ALC than among those with low ALC (86.0% vs. 51.1%, P < 0.001). ALC was identified as an independent factor associated with short-term treatment response by multivariate logistic regression (OR = 4.716, 95% CI: 1.167-19.062, P = 0.030). Longer median OS and PFS were observed in high-ALC patients. In the multivariate Cox analysis, higher ALC remained independently related to improved PFS (HR = 0.450, 95% CI 0.213-0.951, P = 0.036) and improved OS (HR = 0.425, 95% CI 0.184-0.982, P = 0.045). CONCLUSION: Baseline ALC has the potential to be used to guide patient selection and individualized treatment planning, because this readily available biomarker was independently associated with treatment response and survival.

item.title: Prognostic significance of lymph node staging in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Han H, Hou X, Liu Y, Cai W, Jin J, Qiu X, Zhu Z, Zhao K, Hu M, Xue Z
item.description:
Authors: Han H, Hou X, Liu Y, Cai W, Jin J, Qiu X, Zhu Z, Zhao K, Hu M, Xue Z
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1931817
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996502



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nCIT) has emerged as a standard treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This study aimed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) and to assess whether pre-treatment clinical N stage (cN) provides additional prognostic information in patients achieving ypN0. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 194 ESCC patients who received nCIT followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into three groups: cN0/ypN0 (n=104), cN+/ypN0 (n=32), and ypN+ (n=58). Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used for survival analysis. Multivariable models were constructed using a clinically informed variable-selection strategy constrained by the number of events. For the three pairwise comparisons, unadjusted P values were compared against a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold of alpha=0.017 (0.05/3). RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with 31 deaths and 37 recurrences during a median follow-up of 34.0 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier). ypN+ patients had significantly worse overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) than ypN- patients (both Log-rank P<0.001). In the primary multivariable model, ypN+ was an independent adverse prognostic factor for OS (HR = 3.204, 95%CI: 1.563-6.568, P = 0.001) and RFS (HR = 3.780, 95%CI: 1.943-7.356, P<0.001), and remained robust across extended, cycle-adjusted, and landmark sensitivity analyses. Among the three groups, ypN+ showed significantly shorter OS compared with both ypN0 groups (P = 0.002 vs cN0/ypN0; P = 0.008 vs cN+/ypN0; both below the Bonferroni threshold) and shorter RFS compared with cN0/ypN0 (P<0.001). No significant difference was observed between cN0/ypN0 and cN+/ypN0 groups for OS (P = 0.259); the RFS comparison was nominally significant but did not survive Bonferroni correction (HR = 2.799, 95%CI: 1.048-7.479, unadjusted P = 0.040). CONCLUSION: Postoperative ypN stage is the core prognostic determinant in ESCC after nCIT. In patients achieving ypN0, pre-treatment cN did not demonstrate statistically significant additional prognostic discrimination in this cohort, although estimates were imprecise due to the small cN+/ypN0 subgroup and limited events. Postoperative risk assessment should be based primarily on ypN status; these findings require validation in larger, preferably multicenter, cohorts.

item.title: Application of chimeric flaps for complex orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963043
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996499



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal malignancies are rare tumors, and a subset of these patients presents with involvement of the orbitomaxillary area, resulting in a complex maxillectomy defect, which warrants primary reconstruction. Complexity increases with globe preservation, which mandates structural support to the globe, ideally reconstructed using a vascularized osseous flap. Such complex defect reconstruction requires multiple components, which are titrated according to the complex three-dimensional defects. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the outcomes of primary orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy using multicomponent chimeric flaps, which included osseous chimeric flaps for globe-preserving total maxillectomy and soft tissue chimeric flaps for the remaining orbitomaxillary defects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and April 2026 at a tertiary referral center. The cohort included consecutive patients with modified Brown type 3 to 6 maxillectomy defects having sinonasal malignancy, which were primarily reconstructed with chimeric flaps. Data on the pathology, type of orbito maxillectomy defects, and types and components of chimeric flaps were collected. Outcomes were measured by flap survival, re-explorations, wound healing compromise, and delays in the start of adjuvant therapy. Specifically for orbital preservation patients, further assessment was made on the presence of diplopia or enophthalmos. RESULTS: All 11 patients included in the study underwent a chimeric flap for orbitomaxillary defects. The most common pathology was squamous cell carcinoma. Seven (64%) were soft tissue chimeric flaps, and four (36%) were osseous chimeric flaps. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Chimeric flaps with their multiple components, which can be contoured according to the complex three-dimensional orbitomaxillary defects, achieves primary healing. For total maxillectomy with globe preservation, bone reconstruction is warranted. Orbital bone reconstruction use of 3D model for contouring the bone strut and the orbital floor mesh can achieve accurate reconstruction for such complex defects.

item.title: Outcomes of sequential microvascular tissue transfer for radiation induced sequelae post mandibular reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1897431
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996241



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy-related complications following mandibular reconstruction remain a major challenge in head and neck oncologic reconstruction. Although free fibula flap reconstruction has become the gold standard for segmental mandibular defects, delayed radiation-induced sequelae such as hardware exposure, contour deformity, soft tissue atrophy, fistula formation continue to affect long-term outcomes. Literature regarding the role of sequential microvascular tissue transfer in managing these complications remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the indications, surgical planning, recipient vessel selection, and outcomes of sequential microvascular free tissue transfer performed for radiation-induced sequelae after mandibular reconstruction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients who had previously undergone primary mandibular reconstruction using a fibula free flap followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and later developed radiation-related complications requiring secondary microvascular reconstruction were included. Demographic data, primary reconstructive details, radiation parameters, duration between radiation and complication, indications for sequential reconstruction, flap characteristics, recipient vessel selection, postoperative complications, and healing outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Ten patients were included in the study. All patients had undergone primary fibula free flap reconstruction following segmental mandibulectomy followed by sequential microvascular soft tissue reconstruction for radiation induced complications. Ipsilateral superficial temporal vessels were used as recipient vessels in all cases without using vein grafts. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Sequential microvascular reconstruction represents a reliable and effective strategy for managing radiation-induced complications following mandibular reconstruction. Volume loss can be addressed during plate removal surgery which not only achieves a stable soft tissue cover but also prevents further progression to osteoradionecrosis.

item.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome as a candidate correlate and potential predictor of HPV clearance and treatment response after HSIL therapy: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
item.description:
Authors: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1972845
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42991095



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection causes virtually all high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and cervical cancer, but only a minority progress, implicating host and microenvironmental cofactors. The cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM), particularly Lactobacillus-dominated communities, may influence hrHPV persistence, clearance, and response to HSIL treatment. OBJECTIVE: To map evidence linking the CVM with hrHPV clearance and outcomes after HSIL treatment, including loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) and conization, using PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley frameworks. METHODS: Literature on cervicovaginal microbiota, community state types (CSTs), HPV natural history, HSIL/CIN treatment, probiotics, microbiome-directed interventions, and predictive biomarkers was systematically searched and narratively synthesized using a Population-Concept-Context framework. RESULTS: Sixty-six sources were charted. Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated communities (CST-I) were associated with hrHPV clearance and favorable post-treatment outcomes, whereas CST-IV, bacterial vaginosis, and increased alpha-diversity were associated with hrHPV persistence, greater HSIL severity, and treatment failure. Proposed mechanisms include lactic acid-mediated pH regulation, D-lactic acid signaling, and modulation of viral oncoproteins and immune responses. Excision altered the CVM, with restoration of Lactobacillus dominance accompanying viral clearance. Microbial-signature machine-learning models showed promising but preliminary predictive performance. Oral and intravaginal probiotics showed inconsistent but generally favorable trends, with strongest evidence for intravaginal L. crispatus transplantation. Gut microbiome diversity may also influence chemoradiotherapy outcomes in invasive cervical cancer. CONCLUSION: The CVM is a promising predictor of hrHPV clearance and HSIL treatment response. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, and limited prospective evidence restrict clinical translation. Large prospective studies and rigorously designed trials are needed to validate predictive signatures and determine whether microbiome profiling or targeted modulation can improve HSIL management and outcomes.

item.title: PF chemotherapy combined with a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody as first-line treatment in patients with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a prospective, single-arm, phase II clinical study.
item.dc:creator: Liao W, Li Q, Deng Y, Zhang J, Zhao Y, Zhang S
item.description:
Authors: Liao W, Li Q, Deng Y, Zhang J, Zhao Y, Zhang S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1961360
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42990899



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the antitumor activity and safety of cadonilimab, a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) bispecific antibody, combined with platinum/carboplatin and 5-fluorouracil (PF) chemotherapy as first-line treatment for patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC). METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, phase II trial, patients with histopathologically confirmed R/M HNSCC received cadonilimab (10 mg/kg) plus PF chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, followed by maintenance cadonilimab. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS). A target sample size of 30 was planned, but the study was terminated prematurely after enrolling 16 patients due to slow accrual. RESULTS: Sixteen patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 18.4 months (range, 4.6 - 39.6), the 1-year PFS and overall survival (OS) rates were 50.0% (95% CI: 30.6% - 81.6%) and 75.0% (95% CI: 56.5% - 99.5%), respectively. The Objective Response Rate (ORR) was 56.3% (95% CI: 29.9% - 80.2%). Median PFS and OS were 9.8 months (95% CI: 2.8 - NR) and 17.7 months (95% CI: 12.3 - NR), respectively. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in four patients (25%), with no treatment-related deaths or immune-related cardiac toxicities reported. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, first-line cadonilimab combined with PF chemotherapy exhibited potential antitumor activity and manageable safety profiles in patients with R/M HNSCC. Given the favorable baseline profile of the cohort and the single-arm design, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Larger randomized controlled trials are required to determine whether dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade offers an incremental benefit over standard anti-PD-1-based regimens.

item.title: AICAR induces S phase cell cycle arrest in ESCC by targeting the AMPK/mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT pathway.
item.dc:creator: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1975805
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42990857



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: 5-Aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide-1-β-4-ribofuranoside (AICAR), an AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) agonist, exhibits potent antitumor capacity across various malignancies. However, its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remain largely unexplored. METHODS: We treated HEEC, TE1, and TE13 cells with AICAR and assessed proliferation, cell cycle distribution, and expression of key signaling proteins, followed by SN38 cotreatment to evaluate apoptosis and chemosensitization. RESULTS: AICAR treatment suppressed proliferation in all three cell lines but induced a distinct S-phase arrest specifically in ESCC cells. Mechanistically, AICAR activated AMPK, which concurrently inhibited the mTORC1 pathway via TSC2 phosphorylation and activated the mTORC2/AKT pathway through FOXO3-mediated transcriptional upregulation of Rictor. A critical difference was observed between cell types: in HEEC cells, AICAR treatment upregulated the tumor suppressor PTEN, which prevented full AKT activation. In contrast, ESCC cells, with unaltered PTEN and dysfunctional p53, sustained AKT hyperactivation. This drove cells into S-phase, where they were subsequently arrested due to the parallel inhibition of mTORC1. Furthermore, synchronizing ESCC cells in the S-phase with AICAR, followed by its withdrawal and subsequent treatment with SN38, significantly enhanced apoptosis. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal that AICAR induces S-phase arrest in ESCC cells by dually modulating the mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT signaling pathways. This differential effect, stemmed from dysfunctional p53/PTEN axis in ESCC cells, distinguishes ESCC cells from normal epithelial cells. Together, these results suggest that AICAR synchronizes ESCC cells in the S phase, thereby sensitizing them to S-phase-specific agents like SN38 and representing a potential novel strategy for ESCC treatment.

item.title: Machine learning to predict osteoradionecrosis in head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Castro VT, Dalmazo LMT, Reis PEDD, de Abreu WC, Dos Reis RG, Prado-Ribeiro AC, Leite AF, Almeida FT, Guerra ENS
item.description:
Authors: Castro VT, Dalmazo LMT, Reis PEDD, de Abreu WC, Dos Reis RG, Prado-Ribeiro AC, Leite AF, Almeida FT, Guerra ENS
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1955800
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42985507



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Osteoradionecrosis is one of the most severe late adverse effects of head and neck radiotherapy. Predictive models may help identify patients at increased risk and support personalized treatment. This exploratory study aimed to develop a machine learning-based prediction model for osteoradionecrosis in a real-world cohort, following the TRIPOD+AI statement. METHODS: Clinical variables and mandibular dose-volume histogram parameters were collected from head and neck cancer patients treated with radiotherapy. Forward Stepwise Logistic Regression was used for predictor selection. Six machine learning algorithms, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, CatBoost, XGBoost, and TabPFN, were evaluated under class-weighted baseline modelling, threshold optimization, and data augmentation with repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance was primarily assessed using sensitivity. Pairwise comparisons used the Nadeau-Bengio corrected paired t-test with Holm adjustment. RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients were included, of whom 8 developed osteoradionecrosis (8.25%). Of the 80 available variables, V60Gy and tumor location in the oral cavity were selected as predictors. Without augmentation, Logistic Regression achieved the highest sensitivity (0.74 [95% CI: 0.40-1.00]), while several algorithms showed poor sensitivity. With data augmentation, sensitivity ranged from 0.72 to 0.77 across models, with TabPFN, CatBoost, Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine reaching the highest sensitivity. Logistic Regression achieved the highest AUC under both strategies (0.87). However, F1 scores remained modest, reaching a maximum of 0.48. CONCLUSION: Machine learning models demonstrated exploratory potential for ORN risk assessment within an internal validation framework. Class-imbalance strategies were associated with greater minority-class detection in this cohort, but their generalizability remains uncertain. Larger multicenter cohorts and external validation are needed before clinical implementation.

item.title: Real-world clinical outcomes of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1.
item.dc:creator: Fan T, Geng L, Gao G, Long Z, Liu D, Wang Y, Li C
item.description:
Authors: Fan T, Geng L, Gao G, Long Z, Liu D, Wang Y, Li C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1896229
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42979652



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1) is generally managed by observation because spontaneous regression is common and progression to high-grade disease is uncommon. Nevertheless, some patients with persistent HPV infection or repeated low-grade abnormalities may elect active treatment after appropriate counseling. This study aimed to describe the clinical outcomes and safety of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in patients with CIN1 who underwent active treatment. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 269 patients with CIN1 who underwent ALA-PDT at Peking University Shenzhen Hospital between July 2021 and July 2025. All patients received six sessions of ALA-PDT at intervals of 7-14 days. HPV status and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) results were assessed before treatment and during follow-up at 3 months (± 1 month) and, in some patients, at 6 months (± 1 month) after treatment. HPV clearance, cytological improvement, and treatment-related adverse events were analyzed. RESULTS: Among the 266 HPV-positive patients, 155 patients (58.27%) had a negative HPV result at the predefined 3-month follow-up. At 3 months, 205 of 247 patients (83.00%) with available cytological assessment had NILM cytology. No serious adverse events were observed during treatment or follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort study, HPV negativity and improved cytological findings were observed during follow-up after ALA-PDT, together with an acceptable safety profile and no serious adverse events.

item.title: Artificial intelligence in esophageal cancer: a narrative review from a thoracic surgical perspective.
item.dc:creator: Peng D, Liu W, Zhang B
item.description:
Authors: Peng D, Liu W, Zhang B
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1917622
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42979228



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) has potential applications across the esophageal cancer (EC) care pathway, but reported retrospective performance often has not translated into clinically validated decision support. We review the evidence through the lens of thoracic surgical decisions, where the consequences of prediction errors are asymmetric. SCOPE: This narrative review examines AI studies relevant to thoracic surgical decisions, with an emphasis on esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Selected reports were mapped to clinical tasks, analysis units, and validation settings. Supplementary PubMed and Web of Science searches informed the review; studies were selected purposively to illustrate clinical tasks and validation problems, not to represent the entire field. KEY OBSERVATIONS: A randomized endoscopy trial supports improved lesion detection in its study setting. Selected retrospective studies report external testing for nodal risk or pathological response, whereas surgical video and complication models mainly provide internal evaluation. Image-level results, patient-level predictions, and clinical outcomes are distinct. Calibration and prospective pathway evaluation remain necessary before treatment allocation can be based on model output. CONCLUSIONS: AI in EC should presently be considered an investigational decision-support layer rather than a replacement for endoscopic, imaging-based, or multidisciplinary assessment. Translation requires patient-level data partitioning, transparent reporting of calibration and clinical utility, independent external validation, and prospective studies using prespecified decision thresholds.

item.title: Predictors of time to feeding-tube independence in locally advanced head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Salman S, Heppell N, Salman ND, Shirron N, Joseph A, Tsien C, Shenouda G
item.description:
Authors: Salman S, Heppell N, Salman ND, Shirron N, Joseph A, Tsien C, Shenouda G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1956034
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42978687



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prophylactic gastrostomy is widely used during definitive chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced head and neck cancer (LAHNC), yet some patients remain tube-dependent long after treatment. Whether prolonged dependence carries prognostic weight of its own, or simply mirrors tumour burden and performance status, is unclear. We examined predictors of time to feeding-tube independence and the association between persistent dependence and overall survival (OS). METHODS: We reviewed 213 consecutive patients with LAHNC treated at a single institution (2015-2022) with definitive chemoradiotherapy to 70 Gy and prophylactic PEG/RIG placement. Nine patients with an inconsistent extraction date were excluded, leaving 204. Time to independence was analysed with Kaplan-Meier estimates and cause-specific multivariable Cox regression, treating death as a competing risk, with a Fine-Gray sensitivity model. Dosimetric variables and baseline Karnofsky performance status (KPS) were modelled continuously. To avoid immortal-time bias, OS was assessed with landmark analyses at 3, 6 and 12 months. Patients were classified by tube status at each landmark, with adjustment for KPS, T and N classification, smoking history and age. RESULTS: Median time to independence was 3.2 months. Any smoking history predicted slower independence (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.42-0.84; p=0.004), and higher KPS predicted faster independence (HR 1.02 per point, 95% CI 1.01-1.04; p=0.006). Higher middle pharyngeal constrictor dose was associated with slower recovery (HR 0.98 per Gy, 95% CI 0.96-1.00; p=0.048), and oral cavity dose showed a similar trend (p=0.067). In unadjusted landmark analyses, patients still dependent had worse OS at 6 months (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.01-3.13) and 12 months (HR 2.53, 95% CI 1.30-4.91). After adjustment, the association was attenuated and non-significant at 3 months (aHR 1.35, 95% CI 0.76-2.42) and 6 months (aHR 1.48, 95% CI 0.81-2.70), but persisted at 12 months (aHR 2.20, 95% CI 1.05-4.58; p=0.036). CONCLUSIONS: Early tube dependence largely reflects baseline disease burden and performance status. Dependence persisting to one year, however, identifies patients with worse survival that these factors do not explain, and they may merit closer follow-up. Smoking history and middle constrictor dose are potentially modifiable contributors to slower recovery, supporting structured smoking-cessation care and dysphagia-optimised planning. Prospective validation is warranted.

item.title: Implementation of a structured early oral supportive-care pathway and early oral health recovery after oral cancer resection and free-flap reconstruction: a prospective observational cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Huang TM, Chen YC, Cheng YC, Yeh CY, Chang YK, Nian MW, Chiang TI, Tsai SC
item.description:
Authors: Huang TM, Chen YC, Cheng YC, Yeh CY, Chang YK, Nian MW, Chiang TI, Tsai SC
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1981326
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42978609



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing oral cancer resection and free-flap reconstruction often have limited capacity for independent oral hygiene during the immediate postoperative period. Standardized bedside oral supportive-care pathways may help organize early postoperative care, but their implementation and accompanying early oral-health recovery have not been well characterized prospectively. METHODS: This prospective, single-center observational cohort study included 36 adults undergoing oral cancer resection with free-flap reconstruction who received a structured early postoperative oral supportive-care pathway beginning on the day of surgery. The primary outcome domains for the present manuscript were pathway implementation, short-term tolerability, and early oral-health recovery from postoperative day 3 (POD3) to POD13. Clindamycin-based and chlorhexidine-based formulations were both used in routine clinical care and were not assigned by the research team; formulation-specific comparisons were secondary and exploratory. RESULTS: All 36 participants completed both Oral Assessment Scale for Post-Operational Patients with Oral Cancer (OASPOCa) assessments, and 32 (88.9%) were recorded as completing all scheduled daily oral-care sessions in the archived adherence record; four participants had one missed-session record. No clinically significant formulation-related intolerance or discontinuation was recorded. Mean total OASPOCa score decreased from 14.97 (SD 2.79) on POD3 to 11.44 (SD 1.65) on POD13, corresponding to a mean within-participant improvement of 3.53 points (SD 3.15; 95% CI, 2.46-4.59; P < 0.001). At least some participants improved in each of the 10 OASPOCa domains, while others remained unchanged or worsened. In secondary exploratory analyses, the between-formulation difference in mean improvement was 0.39 points (95% CI, -1.78 to 2.55; P = 0.717). CONCLUSION: The structured pathway was implemented with high recorded participant-level adherence and was accompanied by multidimensional early oral-health recovery; no clinically significant formulation-related intolerance or discontinuation was recorded. Because oral care began before the first formal assessment and no untreated or usual-care control group was included, the observed change represents temporal postoperative recovery rather than causal pathway efficacy. No clear overall advantage of either routinely used oral-care formulation was demonstrated.

item.title: Duration of Closed Lock Is Associated With Worsening Clinical Outcomes in Arthroscopic Disc Repositioning Surgery.
item.dc:creator: Sang Y, Danquah S, Lee S, Guastaldi FPS, Choi DD
item.description:
Authors: Sang Y, Danquah S, Lee S, Guastaldi FPS, Choi DD
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.004
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42982096



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-articular pain and dysfunction of the temporomandibular joint includes disc displacement disorders that may progress to prolonged closed lock. Progressive disc deformation and joint degeneration may limit the effectiveness of arthroscopic disc repositioning, but the relationship between locking duration and clinical outcomes remains unclear. PURPOSE: To measure the association between the duration of closed lock and changes in overall jaw function, pain, and maximal incisal opening after arthroscopic disc repositioning. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Massachusetts General Hospital 2023/4 - 2026/1. The study sample included patients with a closed lock who underwent arthroscopic disc repositioning. Subjects with incomplete data or repeated procedures were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: Locking duration recorded as months between patient-reported onset of closed lock symptoms and surgery. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE(S): Primary outcome was 3-month change in Jaw Functional Limitation Scale (JFLS) score; higher scores indicate greater functional limitation. Secondary outcomes were 3-month changes in pain (0 to 10, lower scores indicate less pain) and maximal incisal opening (mm). COVARIATES: Covariates included demographics (age, sex) and perioperative variables (unilateral vs bilateral involvement and Wilkes stage). ANALYSES: Associations of study covariates with locking duration and 3-month JFLS change were evaluated using Spearman's rank correlation, Wilcoxon rank-sum, or Kruskal-Wallis tests. Univariable and multivariable linear regression were used to evaluate the association between locking duration and 3-month JFLS change. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05. RESULTS: The cohort included 38 subjects with established closed lock involving 42 temporomandibular joints; the median age was 27.5 years (Q1, Q3, 20.0, 40.0 years), and 37 subjects (97.4%) were female. Each additional month of locking duration was associated with a 0.153-point smaller 3-month JFLS change in unadjusted analysis (95% CI, -0.285 to -0.021; P = .025). After adjustment for preoperative JFLS score and age, each additional month remained associated with a 0.125-point smaller JFLS change (95% CI, -0.236 to -0.013; P = .03). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Longer locking duration was associated with poorer short-term functional improvement after arthroscopic disc repositioning. Locking duration may be useful when counseling subjects and considering the timing of surgery after unsuccessful conservative management.

item.title: Clinical Efficacy of Pentoxifylline, Tocopherol, and Clodronate Therapy for Osteoradionecrosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Woliansky M, Chen C, Badlani J
item.description:
Authors: Woliansky M, Chen C, Badlani J
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.005
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 42976940



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) of the jaws is a complication of radiation therapy whose most appropriate treatment has been considered and debated in the international literature for several decades. Pentoxifylline, tocopherol, and clodronate (PENTOCLO) therapy shows promise for the management of ORN, but clinical evidence remains scientifically unsubstantiated.
