PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of PENTOCLO for head and neck cancer-related ORN, focusing on mucosal healing and treatment duration to inform future randomized controlled trials. DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE via PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for articles published between 2005 and August 2025. STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies were peer-reviewed, English-language articles evaluating subjects with head and neck cancer-related ORN treated primarily with PENTOCLO. Case reports, expert opinions, and abstract-only publications were excluded. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyse guidelines, 2 reviewers extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions. Published aggregate survival data were used to reconstruct individual-level time-to-event and censoring data, which were pooled to generate Kaplan-Meier survival models. MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Complete mucosal healing, analyzed as a time-to-event outcome, to estimate the median time to healing and cumulative healing trajectories. RESULTS: Six observational studies were eligible (N = 303 total subjects; n = 192 receiving PENTOCLO; mean age: 55.0 to 65.0 years; 78.5% male). Three studies provided reconstructible time-to-event data for Kaplan-Meier pooling (n = 99 research subjects). Pooled median time to complete mucosal healing was 9.0 (interquartile range: 6.0 to 28.0) months, with the unhealed proportion declining from 70.7% at 6 months to 6.3% at 36 months. Complete healing ranged from 35.2 to 100%; pathological fractures averaged 40.1 months of therapy. Risk of bias was serious (n = 3) to critical (n = 3), with no untreated control groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Subjects receiving PENTOCLO demonstrated progressive mucosal healing. However, lacking comparative control cohorts, these observational findings describe single-arm healing trajectories rather than comparative efficacy, underscoring the need for randomized controlled trials.

item.title: Oral versus intravenous melphalan for autologous stem cell transplantation conditioning in lymphoma and multiple myeloma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Wang J, Guo Y, Zhao J, Wen X, Su L, Hao Z, Yang J
item.description:
Authors: Wang J, Guo Y, Zhao J, Wen X, Su L, Hao Z, Yang J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1923679
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42973770



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare oral (PO) and intravenous (IV) melphalan as conditioning regimens for autologous stem cell transplantation in patients with lymphoma or multiple myeloma (MM). METHODS: A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort analysis of 106 patients (76 with lymphoma and 30 with MM) was conducted to compare engraftment outcomes, adverse events, and survival between PO and IV melphalan conditioning. The primary endpoint was 3-year progression-free survival. RESULTS: The BEAM (carmustine, etoposide, cytarabine, and melphalan) regimen is the standard conditioning regimen for lymphoma and a single-agent melphalan was administered for MM. In patients with lymphoma, IV melphalan was associated with faster neutrophil engraftment than PO melphalan (10 vs 12 days, p = 0.025). In MM, IV melphalan was associated with faster platelet (PLT) engraftment (11 vs 14 days, p = 0.021). The PO group had higher grade 3-4 anemia (37.74% vs 18.87%, p = 0.031) but lower febrile neutropenia (35.85% vs 56.60%, p = 0.032) and mucositis (7.55% vs 33.96%, p = 0.001). In the PO group, grade 3-4 anemia correlated with delayed PLT engraftment (62.5% vs 21.4%, p = 0.008). Compared with IV melphalan, divided-dose oral melphalan was associated with lower rates of diarrhea (18.87% vs 37.74%) and oral mucositis (7.55% vs 33.96%), with an overall gastrointestinal toxicity rate (defined as at least one gastrointestinal adverse event) of 21.7% in the PO group versus 56.60% in the IV group. Complete response rates and 3-year survival outcomes were comparable between the groups. CONCLUSION: Oral melphalan is a pragmatic alternative when IV melphalan is unavailable, with comparable efficacy and a distinct toxicity profile. Given variable bioavailability, it should not be considered bioequivalent to IV melphalan. Prospective pharmacokinetic studies are warranted to validate these findings.

item.title: Machine learning-assisted chemometric analysis of salivary ATR-FTIR spectra for the diagnosis of oral submucous fibrosis.
item.dc:creator: Shree P, Aggarwal Y, Kumar M, Saxena P, Singh NN, Chandra A, Srivastava P, Nag S, Rai A
item.description:
Authors: Shree P, Aggarwal Y, Kumar M, Saxena P, Singh NN, Chandra A, Srivastava P, Nag S, Rai A
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1927981
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42973765



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSMF) is a chronic, potentially malignant disorder strongly linked to areca nut chewing. Clinical diagnosis is challenging, and histopathology, though the gold standard, is invasive and subject to inter-observer variability. Saliva analysis using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy offers a promising non-invasive alternative. This study evaluated salivary ATR-FTIR spectral analysis integrated with machine learning for classification of OSMF, individuals with adverse oral habits, and healthy controls. METHODOLOGY: Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 450 participants comprising 150 patients with clinically diagnosed OSMF, 150 individuals with adverse oral habits without clinical evidence of OSMF, and 150 healthy controls. After centrifugation, the saliva supernatant was analyzed by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy over 400-4000 cm-¹. Spectra underwent baseline correction and normalization followed by Savitzky-Golay smoothing. For machine-learning analysis, Standard Scaler and PCA were incorporated within the classification pipeline. Decision Tree, Random Forest, support vector machine (SVM), and XGBoost classifiers were evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Hyperparameter optimization and performance estimation used the same cross-validation framework. An independent cohort of 90 participants was used for validation. RESULTS: XGBoost showed the highest cross-validation performance, with accuracies of 90.62% for Normal versus Habit, 97.67% for Normal versus OSMF, and 91.30% for three-class classification. Statistical analysis identified 157 nominally significant wavenumbers (p<0.05) within a continuous region from 1581 to 2142 cm-¹ corresponding to protein and collagen bands. Principal component analysis showed that PC1 and PC2 explained 89.26% and 6.95% of the total variance, respectively (96.21% cumulatively). In the independent validation cohort, accuracy was 80.0% for OSMF versus Normal and 71.7% for Habit versus Normal. CONCLUSION: Salivary ATR-FTIR combined with machine learning demonstrated promising classification performance and preliminary performance in an independent cohort. The identified spectral region is biologically plausible in the context of altered salivary biochemical composition associated with inflammation and fibrosis, but it should not be regarded as a validated disease-specific biomarker. Salivary ATR-FTIR is best considered a complementary, non-invasive screening and risk-stratification approach rather than a replacement for clinical/oral examination or histopathological assessment when biopsy is indicated. Larger, diverse, multicenter studies with rigorous validation are needed before clinical implementation.

item.title: Temporal variation in initial UICC stage and post-diagnostic treatment intervals in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma in Saxony before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
item.dc:creator: Stach G, Lauer G, Farahzadi S, Schröder TA, Buckova M
item.description:
Authors: Stach G, Lauer G, Farahzadi S, Schröder TA, Buckova M
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1770029
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42973562



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant tumor for which early diagnosis and timely treatment are important determinants of prognosis. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery and reduced participation in preventive examinations. This study examined temporal differences in initial tumor stage and post-diagnostic treatment intervals among patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma. METHODS: This retrospective registry-based study included 3,216 patients diagnosed with oral squamous cell carcinoma between 1 January 2018 and 5 August 2024. Patients were categorized into the pre-pandemic period, the early pandemic period, and the later pandemic period according to their date of diagnosis. Initial UICC stage and post-diagnostic treatment intervals were compared between the three predefined periods and additionally analyzed according to year of diagnosis. Descriptive statistics and non-parametric statistical tests were applied. RESULTS: The distribution of initial UICC stages differed between the three predefined periods, with a higher proportion of stage IV disease in the pre-pandemic period; however, the association was weak. Significant differences between the predefined periods were also identified for the interval from diagnosis to the first multidisciplinary tumor board and for the intervals from the tumor board to surgery with and without subsequent radiotherapy. In the year-by-year analysis, differences were observed in initial UICC stage and in the intervals from diagnosis to the tumor board and from the tumor board to surgery with subsequent radiotherapy. No significant year-by-year difference was observed for the interval from the tumor board to surgery without subsequent radiotherapy. Overall, the annual patterns were non-linear. CONCLUSION: No prolongation of the evaluated post-diagnostic treatment intervals was observed during the early pandemic period compared with the pre-pandemic period. However, the differences in initial UICC stage and selected treatment intervals were small, and the additional year-by-year analysis demonstrated non-linear temporal variation. The findings should therefore be interpreted as temporal associations rather than as evidence of a causal adverse or beneficial effect of the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil-dependent hepatic stellate cell activation.
item.dc:creator: Tang D, Wei J, Liu M, Cui L, Chen J, Li H, Lin M, Li X, Ou Q, Li Q
item.description:
Authors: Tang D, Wei J, Liu M, Cui L, Chen J, Li H, Lin M, Li X, Ou Q, Li Q
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78008-8
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42988798



Abstract:
Periodontitis is a key driver in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Nevertheless, how specific periodontal pathogens contribute to liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we identify Tannerella forsythia as the crucial mediator in the link between periodontitis and liver fibrosis, which can translocate to the gut and aggravate liver fibrosis. Mechanistically, Tannerella forsythia promotes the infiltration of ICAM-1+ neutrophils and inflammatory response in the liver via disrupting intestinal barrier integrity. ICAM-1+ neutrophils secrete TNF-α, which activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway in hepatic stellate cells, triggering collagen deposition and fibrogenesis. Conditional knockout of ICAM-1 in neutrophils or global deletion of TNF-α significantly attenuates inflammatory response and liver fibrosis caused by Tannerella forsythia. Taken together, this study identifies an oral-gut-liver axis driven by Tannerella forsythia and provides a prospective therapeutic target for periodontitis-related liver fibrosis.

item.title: Characterization of silk-like materials from larval salivary glands of the dipteran, Keroplatus testaceus.
item.dc:creator: Kmet P, Opelka J, Lopes TBF, Sehadova H, Sauman I, Hradilova M, Humenik M, Zurovec M
item.description:
Authors: Kmet P, Opelka J, Lopes TBF, Sehadova H, Sauman I, Hradilova M, Humenik M, Zurovec M
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78291-5
Published: 2026-Oct-05
PMID: 42971977



Abstract:
Silk-like secretions are well-studied in many insects but remain poorly characterized in Diptera. Larvae of the dipteran Keroplatus testaceus produce two distinct silk-like materials-a mucus web and a cocoon-from their labial salivary glands, differing in composition and function. Here we combined histology, transcriptomics, electron microscopy, proteomics, mechanical testing, and FTIR spectroscopy to characterize these secretions. Neither contains fibroin; instead, both comprise hydrophilic proteins including collagen-like, mucin, and novel proline-rich proteins. Structural predictions and FTIR analyses reveal β-sheets, α-helices, and polyproline II helices, contributing to mechanical robustness despite high hydration. The mucus web facilitates larval mobility and spore capture, while the cocoon provides mechanical protection during pupation. These findings reveal a fibroin-independent silk system adapted to humid, microbe-rich environments, expanding understanding of insect silk diversity and offering insights into novel biomaterials.

item.title: Spatial control of karyopherin binding avidity within NPC mimics revealed by designer FG-nucleoporins.
item.dc:creator: de Vries HW, Barth A, Fragasso A, Otto TA, van den Berg A, van der Sluis EO, van der Giessen E, Veenhoff LM, Dekker C, Onck PR
item.description:
Authors: de Vries HW, Barth A, Fragasso A, Otto TA, van den Berg A, van der Sluis EO, van der Giessen E, Veenhoff LM, Dekker C, Onck PR
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77818-0
Published: 2026-Sep-28
PMID: 42982848



Abstract:
Nucleocytoplasmic transport occurs via nuclear pore complexes (NPCs), ~40-60 nm wide pores lined with intrinsically disordered proteins that are rich in Phe-Gly motifs (FG-Nups) that form a selective barrier. Molecules larger than ~50 kDa are increasingly blocked for transport unless they are bound to a nuclear transport receptor such as the karyopherin (Kap) family of proteins. How the amino acid sequence of FG-Nups contributes to this selectivity is not fully understood. Here, we present de novo designed artificial FG-Nups with a systematically varied FG-repeat spacing and charge-to-hydrophobicity ratio (C/H). Starting from a reference sequence termed NupY (with the average properties of yeast GLFG-Nups), we design, synthesize, and experimentally test a library of NupY variants using quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring and phase separation assays. We find that the spacing between FG-motifs governs Kap95 absorption into the FG-Nup phase, while increasing C/H results in higher avidity for Kap95 due to an increased accessibility of FG-motifs. Molecular dynamics simulations of transport through NupY-coated pores show a reduced barrier function for noncohesive variants and the highest transport selectivity for designs close to native GLFG-Nups. We postulate that a balance between steric hindrance and enthalpic gain from multivalent Kap-FG-Nup interactions drives the spatial and temporal partitioning of Kaps in the NPC.

item.title: Risk factors for reoperation in patients hospitalized with odontogenic infection-a single center study.
item.dc:creator: Kaercher D, Schieren I, Thelen P, Li L, Hamprecht A, Ruettermann M
item.description:
Authors: Kaercher D, Schieren I, Thelen P, Li L, Hamprecht A, Ruettermann M
Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.09.010
Published: 2026-Sep-22
PMID: 42998963



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Odontogenic infections are common in oral and maxillofacial surgery. In some patients, further surgical drainage is needed. This study evaluated risk factors for reoperation in hospitalised patients with odontogenic infections. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective, single-centre cohort study was conducted in 1,173 hospitalised patients treated for odontogenic infections between January 2014 and April 2020. Patients were divided into a reoperation group (n = 38) and a no-reoperation group (n = 1,135). RESULTS: Chronic renal failure (OR: 5.985, 95% CI: 2.174-16.475; P < .001), chronic respiratory disease (OR: 2.51, 95% CI: 1.031-6.261; P = .043), parapharyngeal space involvement (OR: 4.09, 95% CI: 1.873-8.943; P < .001), and buccal space 1 involvement (OR: 3.431, 95% CI: 1.283-9.179; P = .014) were associated with reoperation in univariable analysis. In multivariable analysis, parapharyngeal space involvement remained the strongest independent predictor (OR: 4.192, 95% CI: 1.676-10.487; P = .002). Admission C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with reoperation in the available laboratory subset (OR: 1.064, 95% CI: 1.034-1.096; P < .001), but this should be interpreted cautiously because values were not available for all reoperated patients. CONCLUSIONS: Parapharyngeal space infection was the main predictor of reoperation. Chronic renal failure and chronic respiratory disease may increase risk. Admission C-reactive protein was associated with reoperation, but the small dataset limits interpretation.

item.title: Integrative genomic and biophysics analysis of MAPK1 rs1057519911 in cervical cancer: genetic association and therapeutic implications.
item.dc:creator: Hassan N, Ullah A, Khan NU, Jan Z, Ahmad W, Albasher G, Al Sultan N
item.description:
Authors: Hassan N, Ullah A, Khan NU, Jan Z, Ahmad W, Albasher G, Al Sultan N
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16946-8
Published: 2026-Sep-18
PMID: 42983332



Abstract:
Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection-related cervical cancer is mostly connected with dysregulated MAPK1 signaling, where genetic variations may alter protein function and affect treatment responses. This study examined the potential treatment implications of the oncogenic missense mutation rs1057519911 in the Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase-1 (MAPK1) gene in relation to cervical cancer susceptibility. The Tetra-ARMS PCR method was used to genotype 300 participants, comprising 100 HPV-positive patients, 100 HPV-negative patients, and 100 healthy controls. The CT and TT genotypes of MAPK1 rs1057519911 were significantly linked with increased odds of cervical disease, mainly in HPV-positive patients (CT: OR = 15.77, 95% CI: 6.80-36.54; TT: OR = 180.95, 95% CI: 37.99-861.93; both P < 0.001). The T allele was also significantly linked with HPV-negative (OR = 8.73, 95% CI: 5.28-14.44) and HPV-positive disease (OR = 15.22, 95% CI: 9.10-25.46; both P < 0.001), supporting an association between the MAPK1 rs1057519911 variant and cervical disease, mostly HPV-positive disease. The rs1057519911 variant results in an E322K amino acid mutation in MAPK1, prompting further structural and dynamic analyses to evaluate its impact on inhibitor binding. Molecular docking analysis of literature-reported MAPK1 inhibitors against both the wild-type and E322K mutant proteins identified SCH772984 as the highest-affinity ligand for the mutant protein, showing a binding affinity of -9.7 kcal/mol compared with - 8.8 kcal/mol for the wild-type protein. Following 50 ns molecular dynamics simulations and post-MD analyses such as RMSD, RMSF, β-factor, radius of gyration, SASA, and dynamic cross-correlation, the findings showed that the mutant complex was more stable. Binding free energy calculations showed more favorable binding of SCH772984 to the MAPK1 E322K variant, with net binding energies of -73.18 kcal/mol (MM-GBSA) and - 76.72 kcal/mol (MM-PBSA), compared with - 66.22 and - 61.83 kcal/mol, respectively, for wild-type MAPK1. These results provide the first evidence linking MAPK1 rs1057519911 to cervical cancer susceptibility in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa population and identify SCH772984 as a promising drug candidate for targeted therapy in HPV-associated cervical cancer.

item.title: Prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory and peripheral immune profiles in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
item.description:
Authors: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16883-6
Published: 2026-Sep-04
PMID: 42995540



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) generally has a favorable prognosis, a subset of patients develop aggressive disease associated with poor outcomes. Current risk stratification relies mainly on clinicopathological features, whereas circulating inflammatory and immune biomarkers may provide complementary prognostic information. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune profiles in patients with DTC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 430 patients with pathologically confirmed DTC who underwent surgical resection. Preoperative inflammatory markers, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles were evaluated, and their associations with overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression models. RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls and patients with benign thyroid nodules, patients with DTC exhibited significantly elevated levels of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), thyroglobulin (Tg), and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) (all P < 0.001). Higher levels of SII, Tg, and TgAb were associated with lymph node metastasis and distant metastasis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis identified older age, follicular thyroid carcinoma, lymph node metastasis, distant metastasis, elevated SII, increased Tg and TgAb levels, and higher CD8⁺ T-cell proportion as independent predictors of inferior OS. Kaplan-Meier analyses further demonstrated that higher proportions of CD3+, CD4+, and CD19 + cells and lower proportions of CD56 + cells were associated with improved OS, whereas CD127 + cell proportion showed no significant association with OS. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles provide complementary prognostic information in patients with DTC. Integration of SII, Tg/TgAb levels, and immune profiling may complement existing risk stratification approaches and facilitate individualized postoperative risk assessment and surveillance.

item.title: SLC3A2 identified as a new therapeutic target for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Li R, Cao S, Liu X, Zhao L, Gong C, Liu F, Qiu J, Wu C, Zhao M, Luo J
item.description:
Authors: Li R, Cao S, Liu X, Zhao L, Gong C, Liu F, Qiu J, Wu C, Zhao M, Luo J
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16448-7
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 42995537



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC), which is the most common malignant tumor of head and neck region. Programmed cell death pathways, including the ferroptosis pathway and the disulphide cell apoptotic pathway, have received increasing amounts of attention as potential targets for cancer therapy. However, the features of genes related to disulfidptosis and ferroptosis in HNSCC remain to be investigated. METHODS: We used a random survival forest (RSF) algorithm model, prognostic and immunological effects to screen SLC3A2. Drug sensitivity prediction and single-cell RNA-seq data further confirmed SLC3A2 as a therapeutic target. In addition, we validated SLC3A2 as a therapeutic target for HNSCC through in vitro experiments. RESULTS: In this study, we used TCGA and GEO database from multiple HNSCC cohorts to identify genes associated with disulphide-related cell death. The prognostic and immunological roles of these genes were investigated, and the key gene related to disulfidoptosis and ferroptosis, SLC3A2, was screened. Drug sensitivity prediction and single-cell RNA-seq data both indicate that SLC3A2 is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of HNSCC. Furthermore, our experiments suggest that overexpression of SLC3A2 in the absence of glucose suppress growth of HNSCC. We also found that knock down SLC3A2 could induce growth defects. In addition, we treated cells with a RING1B inhibitor to regulate SLC3A2 mRNA expression, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target in HNSCC. CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that SLC3A2 is a critical target in HNSCC development, providing new targets and research ideas for the treatment of HNSCC.

item.title: Screen-detected health conditions among students in grade 1-9: findings from Timor-Leste's first nationwide school-based screening program.
item.dc:creator: Jin H, Soares RM, Dos Reis Belo J, Soares F, Rosa AS, Mathur A, Cho M
item.description:
Authors: Jin H, Soares RM, Dos Reis Belo J, Soares F, Rosa AS, Mathur A, Cho M
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28730-1
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 42989189



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systematic health data on school-aged children in Timor-Leste have been lacking. The School-Based Primary Health Care Package screened students in Grade 1-9 nationwide in 2025. We describe the conditions detected and assess how far the estimates reflect variation between screeners. METHODS: Programmatic cross-sectional screening analysis of school-level records for 1,387 basic-education schools. Each community health center fielded at least one team consisting of one doctor and two nurses; the doctor performed physical examinations and substance-use assessments and nurses conducted anthropometry, vision and hearing assessments. Findings came from clinical examination or threshold-based tests, none confirmed by a reference standard, and are reported as screen-detected prevalence using assessment-specific denominator. Intracluster correlations and design effects were estimated directly and used for design-based confidence intervals. Inter-screener reliability was assessed by variance-components analysis across the 72 teams, benchmarked against nutritional status, the least judgement-dependent domain. RESULTS: Two hundred sixty-two thousand, four hundred thirty-four students were screened across 1,371 of 1,387 schools. Screen-detected dental caries affected 78,643 students (30.0%; design-based 95% CI 29.0-31.0), low BMI-for-age 53,565 (20.5%) and poor oral hygiene 44,508 (17.0%). Within-school clustering was strong, and municipal effect sizes were negligible after design correction (Cramér's V 0.012-0.028). Between-team variation was concentrated in the dental assessments, performed by the doctors: these showed a mean team effect 3.51 times the instrument-measured benchmark, versus 0.67 for the doctor's seven non-dental assessments (Mann-Whitney p = 0.012). Screen-detected caries ranged from 3.7% to 67.9% across 72 teams, and the screening team explained 43% of referral variance versus 13% for municipality. CONCLUSIONS: Dental caries and low BMI-for-age were the most frequently screen-detected problems. For the dental assessments the screening team accounted for more of the variation than the municipality, and this variation was specific to the dental tasks rather than to the examiners, who were consistent on assessments within their training. Screen-detected caries should be regarded as a lower bound and its municipal pattern not interpreted. Priorities are to calibrate the screening instrument, estimate caries prevalence through a pathfinder survey, and strengthen both preventive and restorative services.

item.title: Dental caries among 12-year-old adolescents in shanghai: a cross-sectional study on prevalence, severity, and associated risk factors.
item.dc:creator: Yang B, Jiang Y, Wang H, Zhang H, Da D, Yu J, Su H, Shi H, Chen Q, Wu Z, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yang B, Jiang Y, Wang H, Zhang H, Da D, Yu J, Su H, Shi H, Chen Q, Wu Z, et al.
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28707-0
Published: 2026-Aug-10
PMID: 42983373



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess the prevalence, severity, and associated factors of dental caries in permanent teeth among 12-year-old adolescents in Shanghai, China. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2021 among 1,305 adolescents from six randomly selected districts. Clinical examinations recorded dental caries (DMFT index), gingival bleeding, dental calculus, pit-and-fissure sealant, and dental crowding. Questionnaires collected data on sociodemographics, oral hygiene, sugar intake, and dental service use. A zero-inflated negative binomial regression model was used to identify factors associated with caries prevalence and severity. RESULTS: Caries prevalence was 27.9% (mean DMFT = 0.61 ± 1.26), with 72.1% caries-free and 17.1% having untreated decay. Caries burden was highly polarized: the top 10% accounted for 60% of total DMFT. In the multivariable ZINB model, female sex, dental crowding, gingival bleeding, and occasional toothache were associated with higher odds of having caries, while pit-and-fissure sealants and positive oral health attitudes were associated with being caries-free. Among affected adolescents, daily flossing, moderate-frequency sugar intake, poor self-rated oral health, and dental calculus were linked to greater caries severity. CONCLUSION: Caries prevalence among 12-year-olds in Shanghai has continued to decline over the past four decades, yet substantial untreated cases and polarization remain. Future strategies should strengthen monitoring and follow-up care for high-risk adolescents, while scaling up sealant coverage and promoting healthy dietary and oral hygiene practices.

item.title: DLGAP1-AS2 knockdown increases chemosensitivity to vandetanib and synergistically inhibits metastatic activity of papillary thyroid cancer cells: experimental and computational approaches.
item.dc:creator: Oskuie SS, Mahdavi SZB, Nikravesh A, Baradaran B, Yari AH, Pourbagherian O, Mokhtarzadeh AA, Oroojalian F
item.description:
Authors: Oskuie SS, Mahdavi SZB, Nikravesh A, Baradaran B, Yari AH, Pourbagherian O, Mokhtarzadeh AA, Oroojalian F
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16511-3
Published: 2026-Aug-07
PMID: 42989125



Abstract:
Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) progression is closely associated with the regulatory roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). The role of DLGAP1-AS2 has been investigated as a potentially oncogenic lncRNA (oncoLnc) in several malignancies; nevertheless, its specific tumorigenic activity in PTC remains largely unexplored.The relative expression of DLGAP1-AS2 was evaluated using FASTQ files and read count data obtained from thyroid cancer (THCA) samples accessible via the SRA and TCGA repositories. Additionally, siRNA transfection was employed to efficiently inhibit DLGAP1-AS2 activity. The effects of DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib on the proliferation and metastatic capability of PTC cells were evaluated using in vitro experiments (MTT, apoptosis analysis, DAPI staining, cell cycle assessment, and scratch & colony formation assays). The gene expressions of Caspase-3, Caspase-9, Bcl2, Bax, p53, CDK1, MMP-3, MMP-9, CD44, and CD133, WNT9B, MAPK10, and CACNA1D were determined using quantitative real-time PCR.Transfection with si-DLGAP1-AS2 resulted in a marked downregulation of DLGAP1-AS2 expression in B-CPAP cells. Treatment with si-DLGAP1-AS2 or vandetanib alone exerted limited effects on B-CPAP cells' viability, whereas their combination exerted marked toxicity against these cells and decreased the IC50 of vandetanib from 44.96 µg/ml to 27.36 µg/ml, reflecting the higher sensitivity of B-CPAP cells to this chemotherapeutic when combined with si-DLGAP1-AS2. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that the combination therapy substantially augmented apoptosis rate, surpassing the level observed in si-DLGAP1-AS2 or vandetanib-treated groups. The sub-G1 cell population increased after si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib individual treatments, yet combination treatment led to a higher sub-G1 ratio. The combined use of si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib markedly impeded cell migration, accompanied by MMP-9 and MMP-3 downregulation. There was a down-expression of stemness-associated markers of CD44 and CD133 measured by qRT-PCR. Pro-apoptotic genes, including Caspase-3, Caspase-9 and Bax, were upregulated while Bcl2, WNT9B, MAPK10, and CACNA1D genes were substantially downregulated in the combined treatment group vs. control group. In conclusion, si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib combination promoted cell cycle arrest by regulating key genes involved in the process. DLGAP1-AS2 seems to be a potential prognostic biomarker involved in the molecular pathogenesis of PTC and a promising candidate for targeted therapy development.

item.title: Immigrant parents' perspectives on healthy growth in children: a qualitative study.
item.dc:creator: Toftemo I, Glavin K, Yogaseelan C, Shakeel N, Jenum AK, Braend A
item.description:
Authors: Toftemo I, Glavin K, Yogaseelan C, Shakeel N, Jenum AK, Braend A
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28788-x
Published: 2026-Aug-07
PMID: 42977947



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In many high-income countries, children with immigrant background exhibit a higher prevalence of obesity, compared to non-immigrant children. We explored the perspectives of immigrant-background parents regarding their children's healthy growth, feeding practices, physical activity, and factors supporting a healthy lifestyle. METHODS: We conducted in-depth interviews with 22 immigrant-background parents living in Southeastern Norway. These parents represented 8 countries of origin and varied widely in terms of length of residence in Norway and educational attainment. The age of their children varied from 3 months to 40 years. Interviews were audiotaped, transcribed verbatim and analysed using a thematic approach. RESULTS: Many informants expressed deep concern about their infants being too small, viewing chubbiness in babies as a sign of health, wealth, and good parenting. Parents and grandparents often encouraged children to eat and fed them by spoon or hand, sometimes well beyond school age. Feeding older children was described as a cultural expression of love and care. While parents recognized the importance of physical activity, high cost of organized sports was a significant barrier. Girls were generally allowed to participate in sports, provided they could wear culturally appropriate sportswear. Parents of children aged 1-5 expressed strong trust in kindergartens to promote healthy lifestyles and saw these institutions as important sources of information about nutrition and physical activity. Building trust in healthcare professionals was often a gradual process. Some parents reported conflicts between professional health advice and views held by family members or social networks. Parents expressed a need for culturally adapted oral and written information, including online resources in their native languages, and access to interpreters and bilingual community leaders. All parents emphasized the need for lower food prices and the provision of daily healthy meals in kindergartens and schools. CONCLUSION: Public health strategies aimed at preventing childhood obesity should be tailored to the specific needs of immigrant families. These strategies might include strengthening the role of kindergartens and schools in providing healthy environments; encouraging collaboration between health and education professionals to address perceptions of healthy child appearance and potentially unfavourable feeding practices; and improving access to organized physical activities by offering financial support and allowing girls to wear culturally adapted sportswear.

item.title: Tumor-stromal ratio as a predictive marker for lymph node metastasis in patients with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma: a cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Muthuvel R, Saheb MIM, A N G, M SK
item.description:
Authors: Muthuvel R, Saheb MIM, A N G, M SK
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16461-w
Published: 2026-Aug-06
PMID: 42983321



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The prognostic potential of the tumor-stromal ratio (TSR) in esophageal, colon, breast, cervical, and oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCC) has been well documented. Lymph node involvement is a critical prognostic factor in oral cavity cancers, and understanding its association with histopathological features may improve prognostic assessments. This study aimed to evaluate the association between TSR and lymph node metastasis (LNM) in patients with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 55 patients diagnosed with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma who underwent upfront surgical treatment. Tumor specimens were assessed for TSR, defined as the proportion of tumor cells relative to the total tumor area (tumor cells plus stroma), using routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. A TSR ≥ 50% was classified as the tumor-rich (high TSR) group, and TSR < 50% as the stroma-rich (low TSR) group. The association between TSR and lymph node metastasis was analyzed using Pearson's chi-square test and Fisher's exact test where appropriate. RESULTS: A significant association was observed between high TSR and the presence of lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001). In the high TSR group (n = 26), 20 patients (76.9%) had lymph node metastasis, compared with 7 patients (24.1%) in the low TSR group (n = 29). The positive predictive value (PPV) was 74.04% and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 78.5%. TSR was also significantly associated with tumor grade (p < 0.001), lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) (p < 0.001), and tumor size (p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: TSR, assessed on routine H&E-stained slides, is significantly associated with lymph node metastasis in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma. It represents a simple, cost-effective histopathological parameter that may aid in predicting nodal spread and informing treatment planning. Further prospective studies with larger cohorts are warranted to validate these findings.

item.title: Multi-omics characterization of CAF-related transcriptional programs reveals a smoking-context-informed 11-gene prognostic signature in HNSCC.
item.dc:creator: Shi T, Wang Y, Yu L, Zhao Y
item.description:
Authors: Shi T, Wang Y, Yu L, Zhao Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16603-0
Published: 2026-Aug-05
PMID: 42972293



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tobacco exposure contributes to the development and progression of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) through genomic damage and alterations in the tumor microenvironment. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are important stromal components of the tumor microenvironment, but the relationships among smoking background, CAF-related transcriptional programs, and clinical outcomes in HNSCC remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize CAF-related transcriptional programs in HNSCC and evaluate their prognostic relevance in the context of smoking status. METHODS: We integrated scRNA-seq data with bulk RNA-seq analyses from TCGA-HNSC, in which smoking-background differential expression analyses were used for candidate-gene discovery. Using hdWGCNA, we identified CAF-associated gene modules and constructed a smoking-related CAF 11-gene (SRCAF-11) signature using machine-learning approaches. We evaluated the signature using external cohorts, immune deconvolution analyses, and SHAP-based feature interpretation. We also modulated INHBA expression in HNSCC cell lines to assess its effects on proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-related features. RESULTS: We identified five transcriptionally distinct CAF subtypes. Matrix-remodeling CAFs (matCAFs) showed extracellular matrix-related features, and higher MuSiC-inferred matCAF relative abundance was associated with poorer survival. Smoker and non-smoker tumors did not differ significantly in MuSiC-inferred CAF-subtype proportions, whereas smoker tumors showed enrichment of EMT- and extracellular matrix-remodeling-related transcriptional programs. The SRCAF-11 signature stratified overall survival across retrospective HNSCC cohorts. INHBA emerged as a major contributor to the model and was preferentially expressed in matCAFs. High INHBA expression was associated with lower inferred immune activity and increased EMT-related transcriptional features in malignant epithelial cells. In vitro, modulation of INHBA expression altered HNSCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial and mesenchymal marker expression, and E-cadherin localization. CONCLUSION: The SRCAF-11 signature showed prognostic stratification capability across retrospective HNSCC cohorts. INHBA was identified as a major model feature associated with p-EMT-related transcriptional characteristics. These findings support a context-dependent association between smoking status, CAF-related transcriptional programs, and aggressive tumor phenotypes in HNSCC. Further mechanistic and spatial validation is required.

item.title: Tumor budding and tumor-associated lymphocytic response as histopathological indicators of high-risk disease in head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Aksu D, Yalçın GŞ, Karasu N, Kuzu S, Özdemir Ç, Aksu U
item.description:
Authors: Aksu D, Yalçın GŞ, Karasu N, Kuzu S, Özdemir Ç, Aksu U
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16653-4
Published: 2026-Aug-04
PMID: 42983664



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor budding (TB) and tumor-associated lymphocytic response (TALR) have emerged as promising histopathological indicators of tumor aggressiveness across epithelial malignancies. Recent studies have suggested that both tumor invasive activity and host immune response contribute substantially to disease progression in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). However, data evaluating their combined significance in head and neck cSCC remain limited. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 187 primary head and neck cSCC cases was analyzed. TB was graded using a three-tier system, and TALR was categorized into three inflammatory response patterns. Associations with clinicopathological characteristics were evaluated using univariate analyses. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with high-risk disease, defined as advanced pathological stage (T3-T4). RESULTS: High-grade TB was significantly associated with adverse histopathological characteristics, including poor differentiation, increased depth of invasion, aggressive invasion pattern, perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and advanced pathological stage (all p < 0.001). Weak TALR was associated with infiltrative growth characteristics and older age. In multivariable analysis, Grade 3 TB (OR 6.75, 95% CI 2.33-19.57), tumor depth > 6 mm (OR 4.03, 95% CI 2.03-8.38), poor differentiation (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.06-6.61), aggressive invasion pattern (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.43-6.60), and weak TALR (OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.12-4.69) remained independently associated with high-risk disease. CONCLUSIONS: Tumor budding and tumor-associated lymphocytic response were independently associated with histopathological features of high-risk disease in head and neck cSCC. Their combined assessment may provide additional information for pathological risk stratification and may support incorporation into routine histopathological evaluation. Prospective studies incorporating recurrence and survival outcomes are required before definitive prognostic conclusions can be established.
